title: Archiving the Present, a network for South Asia’s oral knowledge launches in Kochi before WikiConference India
content:
On 3 September, 37 of us are meeting to learn from each other how we can better document our community stories, voices and knowledge and safe-keep them for long. Most have spent over three months learning together online and will meet in person for the first time.

This is the day OpenSpeaks, together with other collaborators, launches Archiving the Present, a community network for oral knowledge in local languages, a manual and a free course of the same name. The network—individual language documenters, archivists, groups and organisations representing local communities, language archives, media institutions, funders, and others—will support the documentation and archiving of South Asia’s languages.

The network will align with a shared goal—that oral knowledge is human knowledge and deserves to be treated as equal to written knowledge. That means fair recognition and fair pay for the people who hold it.

title: Apple Maps renames Lake Ontario as ‘Lake America’ for US users after Trump order
content:
Tech company submits to controversial Trump order to rename body of water amid US trade spat with Canada

Apple has renamed Lake Ontario as “Lake America” for US users of its Maps app, after an executive order from Donald Trump to change the name of the Great Lake amid his trade spat with Canada.

The Apple Maps app now displays the controversial new name for the lake, which sits between New York state and the Canadian province of Ontario, for users in the US. Apple users outside the country will still see the Lake Ontario name.

title: Vieraskielisten kaupunkilaisten uskonnollisuutta tutkittu: kirkkoa arvostetaan laajasti, jäsenyys harvinaista
content:
Suomessa asuvat vieraskieliset eivät muodosta uskonnollisesti yhtenäistä ryhmää, vaan erot kieliryhmien välillä ovat suuria. Samalla tutkimus osoittaa, että kristillisiä kirkkoja arvostetaan laajasti riippumatta vastaajien omasta uskonnollisesta taustasta, vaikka vain harva harkitsisi liittyvänsä kirkon jäseneksi.

Espoon, Helsingin, Tampereen ja Vantaan seurakuntayhtymien, Kirkkohallituksen sekä Kirkon tutkimuksen toteuttamaan kyselyyn vastasi yli 3 200 vieraskielistä Suomessa asuvaa henkilöä. Nyt julkaistussa tutkimusraportissa tarkasteltiin kuutta suurta kieliryhmää ja niiden välisiä eroja. Vastaajat poimittiin ositetulla satunnaisotannalla väestötietojärjestelmästä keväällä 2026.

Suomessa asuu noin 646 000 vieraskielistä henkilöä. Vieraskielisiksi lasketaan muuta kieltä kuin suomea, ruotsia, saamea, romania tai viittomakieltä äidinkielenään puhuvat. Heistä noin puolet asuu Helsingissä, Espoossa, Vantaalla ja Tampereella, jotka olivat tutkimuksen kohdealueita.

title: Brain, Music, and Learning at the Society for the Neuroscience of Creativity in Philadelphia (USA)
content:
The  (SfNC) promotes research on creativity and provides a forum for sharing research across fields such as innovation, education, health, industry, policy, and the arts. Its scope includes the neural and cognitive bases of creativity, as well as its broader contexts, applications, and outcomes.

The society organizes an annual conference that brings together researchers studying creativity from a neuroscience perspective. The 2026 edition took place in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (USA), on 1–3 June.

Brain, Music, and Learning researchers Tommi Makkonen, Cesc Bayle (attending), and Mari Tervaniemi presented their research on the neuroscience of music improvisation at SfNC26: “Improvisation and the Creative Brain – Advancing Ecologically Valid Music Neuroscience Research.”

title: Kirjastosta lainatuilla vaatteilla mentiin festareille ja kirkkoon
content:
Mitä tarkoittaa merkityksellinen vaatesuhde? kysyy pukusuunnittelija ja taiteilija Onerva Luoma.

Viime kesänä kuukauden ajan ympäri Helsinkiä liikkui ihmisten päällä kirjastokortilla lainattavia vaatteita, joita käytettiin yllättävissä paikoissa aina Suomenlinnasta Voguen kuvauksiin.

Kyseessä oli Luoman käsitetaideteos Vie minut pois täältä (vaikka en tiedä onko sellaista paikkaa). Vaatteet olivat esillä ja lainattavissa Vallilan kirjaston Galleria Kajavassa.

Onerva Luoma on Helsingissä asuva pukusuunnittelija ja taiteilija, joka työskentelee niin teatterin, elokuvan, tekstiilitaiteen kuin eri kuvataiteen eri muotojen parissa.

Vaatteiden laina-aika oli viikko. Lainaaja sai mukaansa ohjeet, joissa pyydettiin muun muassa pesemään vaate ennen palauttamista. Yksi asiakas sai lainata maksimissaan yhden setin, eli kaksi vaatetta.

“Kirjat ovat taideteoksia, joita voi lainata kirjastosta, mutta silti ne ovat enemmän esineitä kuin maalaukset. Teollisesti tuotettu vaate on myös esine. Entä jos vaate olisikin täysin uniikki. Miten se eroaa taideteoksesta?” Luoma kysyy.

title: Mitä lukisit seuraavaksi? Kirjavinkkikiertue Lahden lähikirjastoissa

Lähikirjastojen syksyn kirjavinkkikiertueella on tarjolla monipuolisesti lukuvinkkejä jokaiselle lukijalle.

Aikuisille suunnatussa vinkkauksessa esitellään monipuolisesti kauno- ja tietokirjallisuutta. Mukana on niin kevyttä kuin ajatuksia herättävää luettavaa, uutuuksia ja klassikoita. Vinkkikiertue tarjoaa mahdollisuuden löytää uusia lukuelämyksiä ja kokeilla jotakin tavallisista lukutottumuksista poikkeavaa.

Halutessaan osallistujat voivat myös jakaa omia lukukokemuksiaan ja kirjavinkkejään. Vinkkauksissa esitellään pääosin eri kirjoja, joten mukaan voi tulla useammankin kerran.

title: Der Wendepunkt
content:
Das von Erika Mondria konzipierte Forschungsprojekt Der Wendepunkt mit der Visualisierung MIND_CLOUD verwandelte Besucher*innen nicht nur in Proband*innen, sondern auch in Forschungsexpert*innen in ihrem eigenen Forschungslabor – dem Gehirn. 

Entscheidungsprozesse und Gehirnwellen aus dem privaten, unsichtbaren Schädelinneren im Zuge einer neurowissenschaftlichen Studie im öffentlichen Raum einem breiten Publikum zu präsentieren, schuf neue gesellschaftliche Diskursräume, die fundamentale ethische wie kulturphilosophische Kernfragen berührten. Als zentrale Metapher für die untersuchte Gehirnaktivität im Stirnlappen diente die „MIND_CLOUD“, in der oszillatorische Veränderungen des Gehirns als dynamische Transformationen einer Wolkenlandschaft interpretiert und visualisiert wurden.

title: 3D-4CH reaches the halfway point: building Europe’s 3D digital heritage community
content:
18 months into the project, 3D-4CH has reached an important milestone. The Online Competence Centre in 3D for Cultural Heritage is live, a growing community is coming together around 3D cultural heritage, and new opportunities for learning, collaboration and innovation are taking shape across Europe. With another 18 months ahead, the project is now ready to build on this momentum and turn its foundations into lasting impact.

The first half of 3D-4CH has been about turning a shared vision into something tangible: a European online hub where cultural heritage professionals can learn, discover tools, share knowledge and explore new ways of working with 3D.

Since the launch of the 3D-4CH Online Competence Centre in 3D for Cultural Heritage on 28 January 2026, the platform has continued to grow. At Month 18, it already brings together 7 online courses across 6 thematic modules, 45 tools and 80 Knowledge Base resources, alongside storytelling scenarios, events and news. With multilingual content and automatically generated subtitles for Knowledge Base videos, the Centre is designed to make 3D knowledge more accessible to professionals across Europe.

title: How Leonardo da Vinci’s Procrastination Contributed to His Creativity
content: At the height of their productivity as Beatles, neither Paul McCartney nor John Lennon could read or write music notation. Clearly it didn’t keep them from making a cultural impact, and as with so much else in life, they regarded it humorously. As McCartney has said, they used to liken themselves to ancient Egyptian pharaohs, who relied on scribes rather than being literate themselves. It’s worth considering whether, all things considered, this inability was really a deficiency: not being rigorously schooled in the traditions and conventions of music could have given them just the freedom they needed to create fresh songs. And if you’ve struggled with procrastination, have you considered likening yourself to Leonardo da Vinci?

title: Infrastructure Before Output: How Museum of Toronto Built a Digital Ecosystem by Doing the Wrong Things First
content:
Most conference talks about digital strategy focus on the answer. The ecosystem is in place, the team is aligned, the numbers look good. At a recent MuseumNext event, Davin Henson of Museum of Toronto offered something different: a candid account of the years between having a digital presence and having a digital ecosystem, including the wrong turns, the misleading metrics, and the sequencing principle that finally made the work hold together.

Henson had spoken at MuseumNext in 2021 and 2022 about content strategy and digital distribution. Those were honest talks, he said, but early-stage ones. This time he told the fuller story, structured as three phases and one principle: infrastructure before output, in that order.

title: Can You Read Spanish? Latin? Catalan? The Library of Congress Needs Your Help
content:
Today’s post is from Lauren Algee, a Senior Digital Collections Specialist & By the People community manager at the Library of Congress. 

What can you learn about the history of Spain from a 500-year-old will?  How about a court ruling from the 1700s? These are the questions behind the transcription campaign for the Law Library of Congress’s Spanish Legal Documents collection. 

In 1941, the Library of Congress purchased the materials, as “a collection of covenants of judicial contests between people, noble men and civil and religious institutions in Spain – Reales Cédulas –Pragmáticas Reales of the XVIIth and XVIIIth centuries.” The collection then remained in the Law Library for over 40 years before funds were made available to organize, index, and photograph the documents for microfilm and make them available for public use. The collection was eventually digitized and published online, but aside from English language titles and short descriptions, the Law Library staff still have limited knowledge about the texts or the topics, individuals, and significant historical moments documented within the collection.

content:

The 2026 National Book Festival arrived in style in late August, drawing tens of thousands of bibliophiles, many of whom turned up in festive shirts emblazoned with mottos such as “reading is my favorite sport,” “unreliable narrator,” “sorry, I’m booked” and “bookmarks are for quitters.”

More than 45,000 people attended this year’s event (Aug. 22) at the D.C. convention center, which showcased more than 80 authors and a pavillion full of programs featuring the Library’s collections and resources.

Newlen, in a short speech that opened the festival. “The Library of Congress has more doors to open than any other library in the world and we hope that you will walk through many of them. Today we have the extraordinary privilege of bringing together some of the most compelling writers and thinkers of our time with all of you, the people who love their work.”

title: Texas and Florida Step Back from ALPRs
content:
Within the last few days, two important state actions have dealt a big blow to automated license plate reader (ALPR) networks. This is just the latest proof of the growing tide of public opposition to mass surveillance. After years of successful grassroots battles to pull these cameras from local streets, bipartisan momentum is sweeping the country.

On August 28, Texas Governor Greg Abbott banned state agencies from spending public funds on Flock cameras. The order dropped just as The Texas Tribune prepared to publish an investigation revealing that a state agency had quietly funneled at least $30 million into building a sprawling surveillance network. 

Then on August 31, the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT) issued a memo, announced by Governor Ron DeSantis, ordering the removal of all ALPRs from the right-of-way on state highways within 30 days. The order revokes all previously approved permits to install ALPRs, and bars transportation officials from issuing future permits.

title: Watching 'Buried' with Michael Sheen?
content:
Dear friend,

Have you watched the BBC two-parter Buried, in which actor Michael Sheen follows the evidence around several toxic waste dumps across Wales and England? 

We were very interested to learn that much of the research that informed the programme was obtained via our Freedom of Information site, WhatDoTheyKnow, by a tireless campaigner for the truth — vicar Paul Cawthorne.

We spoke to Paul to learn more about the part FOI has played in bringing this terrible scandal to public attention. Read our conversation here.

This isn’t the first time our sites have played a part in a TV campaign. In October 2023, we spoke to WhatDoTheyKnow user Eleanor Shaikh, who’d uncovered crucial evidence about the Post Office scandal.

In January ’24, the extent of the issue hit the public consciousness via TV series Mr Bates vs the Post Office. You can hear Eleanor explain how she used FOI in this ten minute podcast.

And all the way back in 2011, we built the app for George Martin’s empty homes campaign, the Great British Property Scandal.

That programme is now off air, but you can read more about how we adapted our FixMyStreet codebase so people could report empty buildings in their area.

title: Hey EU, your new rules for ChatGPT don’t cover chat
content:
The EU’s decision to regulate ChatGPT as a search engine will make sense to those who use it as one. But what if you use it as a friend? Or a therapist? Or to have a chat about the upcoming election?  

Those are among the multitude of new questions that the advent of generative AI poses for European regulators — who, experts say, have yet to find sufficient answers.  

The EU executive on Monday designated ChatGPT as a Very Large Online Search Engine under the Digital Services Act, imposing a range of transparency and risk-mitigation obligations similar to those faced by traditional search leaders like Google and Microsoft’s Bing, which exceed 45 million monthly users. ChatGPT’s parent company, OpenAI, risks fines of up to 6% of its annual global revenue if it fails to meet these requirements.

title: Russia: Detention of charity leader Lida Moniava for anti-war social media posts a brazen attack on freedom of expression
content:
Reacting to the detention of Lidiya (Lida) Moniava, a Russian civil society activist and prominent charity leader, for alleged “dissemination of false information” about the Russian Armed Forces, Marie Struthers, Amnesty International’s Director for Eastern Europe and Central Asia, said:

“The criminal case against Lida Moniava is yet another brazen attempt by Russia’s authorities to crackdown on any expression of anti-war sentiment. This assault on one of Russia’s most prominent charity leaders is designed to silence not only her, but the entire civil society.”

“The Russian authorities must immediately end the criminal prosecution of Lida Moniava for peacefully exercising her right to freedom of expression. They must repeal the country’s repressive ‘war censorship’ legislation and release all those imprisoned solely for the peaceful exercise of their right to express opposition to the war.”

title: Cambodia Court Sentences 3 Activists to 7 Years in Prison
content:
The government-controlled municipal court in Phnom Penh on September 2, 2026 sentenced three activists to seven years in prison for allegedly plotting against the government. They were 25-year-old student leader Thy Thorn and two political opposition activists, Soeung Kunthea and Mean Chanthon. Kunthea and Chanthon were arrested in Thailand in November 2024 and summarily deported to Cambodia to face trial, despite being recognized as refugees by the United Nations refugee agency.

The long sentences on baseless charges are the latest abuse of the judicial system by the ruling Cambodian People’s Party in its efforts to silence critical voices in the country.

Thorn, Chanthon and Kunthea were among at least 94 people arrested by Cambodian authorities in 2024 amid a wave of criticisms of the Cambodia–Laos–Vietnam Development Triangle Area (CLV), a controversial economic development plan among the three governments established in 2004. The Cambodian government later withdrew from the agreement after the public outcry.

title: Ben Okri—a Great Novelist and an Immigrant—Hits Out
content:
By Jonathan Power

LUND, Sweden | 2 September 2026 (IDN) — “In the beginning there was a river. The river became a road, and the road branched out to the whole world. And because the road was once a river it was always hungry.”

This must be one of the best opening lines ever penned by a novelist. It’s the work of the Nigerian novelist, Ben Okri, who won English literature’s premier annual award, the Booker Prize, for his book, The Famished Road.

It’s an exceptional novel. The words are often thrown up in the air and then, catching the sun’s rays, light up like emeralds, rubies, diamonds, gold and silver as they tumble down onto the page.

When I met Ben Okri at Denmark’s annual literary festival at the Louisiana Museum of Modern Art, I wanted to ask him how it is that Nigeria has become a veritable factory of good novelists. Besides the Nobel Prize winner for literature, Wole Soyinka, there has been Chinua Achebe with his “Things Fall Apart,” which schoolchildren all over the world read. Today, two great women writers stand out: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie and Helen Oyeyemi. Every five or six months, another good novelist emerges.

title: Finland’s berry industry shifted from Thai pickers to Nepalese students, but exploitation remains unchecked
content:
The exploitation of foreign wild berry pickers in Finnish forests continues, and most of them still work without the security provided by an employment contract. 

Instead of Thai farmers travelling to Finland for the harvest season of blueberries and other wild berries, which was the setup for two decades and resulting in human trafficking, the work in the forests is now being carried out by foreign nationals already residing in the country. According to information acquired by Faktabaari, the workers are mostly higher education students from Nepal and elsewhere from South Asia. 

Reports from the Finnish occupational safety and health authorities and Victim Support Finland show the pickers have faced similar problems to those in previous years: they have reported low earnings after various costs have been deducted from their wages, as well as inadequate accommodation and food. Pickers have also been charged ‘entry fees’ which have not subsequently been refunded.

title: How the Hell Did an Island Suddenly Appear, Then Vanish?
content:
An island that appeared to suddenly materialize, then vanish, on Williston Lake in British Columbia over the summer was rediscovered on the massive reservoir on Monday. 

Once you’ve taken that all in, let’s ask the important question: How the heck did that happen? 

The existence of the disappearing island—a floating mass of trees and vegetation that measures about 230 feet by 460 feet—sparked international attention last month after Rocky Avery, a local resident, posted a viral video of it that was sent to him by one of his boater friends, according to CBC News.

Bob Gammer, a spokesperson for BC Hydro, was initially suspicious that the video might be AI, but confirmed it was authentic after spotting the island drifting about 60 miles west of the W.A.C. Bennett Dam in satellite images taken on July 21. In satellite images from August 5th and circulated last week, it was no longer visible, sparking a search over the past few days that led to its rediscovery about 20 miles northwest of where it had previously been spotted.
snippet: An island that appeared to suddenly materialize, then vanish, on Williston Lake in British Columbia over the summer was rediscovered on the massive reservoir on Monday.

title: Businessman Acquitted of Commissioning Murder of Maltese Journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia
content:
Nine years after investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia was killed by a car bomb outside her home in Malta, businessman Yorgen Fenech has been found not guilty of complicity for allegedly masterminding her assassination.

The nine-member jury returned its verdict on the evening of September 2 after about 8 hours of deliberation, voting 8-1 on the charge of complicity and 8-1 on the other charge he faced for alleged criminal association. 

The verdict at the Law Courts in Valletta, Malta's capital, closes what has been one of the longest jury trials in the country’s history, running to 55 sitting days since it opened on July 1.

Fenech, 44, the former chief executive of the Tumas Group, had pleaded not guilty. 

The prosecution, led by Anthony Vella and Godwin Cini, is expected to appeal the verdict. It argued that Fenech commissioned and financed the killing, paying self-confessed middleman Melvin Theuma 150,000 euros ($ 170,00) to engage the hitmen, and that he passed Theuma information about the police investigation in the two years that followed. Theuma was granted a presidential pardon to testify in the case.

title: New Mail Voting Rules Moved Forward Despite USPS Officials’ Concerns About Mass Disenfranchisement
content:
Top U.S. Postal Service officials tasked with issuing new regulations on mail voting expressed concerns in internal meetings about how the rules they were drafting could delay or block ballots from reaching large swaths of eligible voters for the upcoming midterms, but the rules moved forward anyway, ProPublica has learned.

The revelations about the discussions, from someone familiar with the rulemaking process, come as a separate anonymous federal employee filed a whistleblower disclosure with U.S. Sen. Richard Blumenthal, warning that the new system is untested and error-prone, and could lead to mass disenfranchisement in the upcoming election. The whistleblower described the entire process as “secretive, rushed, chaotic, and fundamentally flawed.”

title: Is Germany’s far right AfD about to take over a state government for the first time?
content:
Germans in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt will go to the polls on September 7 to elect a new parliament.

With forecasts indicating that the Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) is on course to win around 40% of the vote, which would double its support there compared to five years ago, there is a real chance the far-right party could take over a state government for the first time.

Former East Germany, which was under Communist rule between 1949 and 1989, has proven fertile ground for the far right. The AfD won 34.6% of the vote there in the 2025 federal election, while in Saxony-Anhalt that figure was 37.1%. This was far higher than mainstream parties on the left and right.

Much has been written about the reasons for far-right success in eastern Germany. Deindustrialisation, demographic change and depopulation, especially in rural areas, are all drivers. So too is the fact there is far stronger disagreement in the east with Germany’s support for Ukraine in its war with Russia than is in evidence in the west, as well as higher levels of opposition to refugees.

title: Moni siirtolainen haaveilee muutosta ”länteen”, vaikka riskit ovat tiedossa – Tutkija Saroj Koirala halusi ymmärtää, miksi, ja teki väitöskirjan
content:
Kun tutkija Saroj Koirala kävi lukiota, lähes kaikki hänen opiskelutoverinsa puhuivat samasta asiasta: siitä, mihin maahan he lähtisivät opiskelemaan.  

Lähteminen vaikutti Koiralastakin järkevältä. Monilla, myös hänellä, oli sukulaisia, jotka olivat lähteneet Nepalista ja pärjänneet hyvin ulkomailla. Niinpä hänkin lähti.

Ikätovereiden suosikkikohdemaa oli Yhdysvallat, mutta Koirala valitsi Norjan, jonne tunkua oli vähemmän ja jossa opiskelu oli tuolloin ilmaista. Hän haki yliopistoon koulutusalan konsulttifirman avustuksella ja aloitti opinnot siellä vuonna 2009. 
 
Tämän vuoden elokuussa Koirala väitteli tohtoriksi Jyväskylän yliopistosta aiheesta, jota hän on pohtinut myös henkilökohtaisesti: miksi niin moni nepalilainen valitsee saman tien kuin hän ja lähtee ulkomaille? 

Siirtolaisuustutkimuksessa on selvitetty sitä itse asiassa paljonkin, mutta Koiralalla oli mielessään myös toinen kysymys. 

”Miksi ihmiset lähtevät riskeistä huolimatta ja vaikka tulos on epävarma?” 

Tavallisesti töihin tai opiskelemaan lähtemistä selitetään tutkimuksissa taloudellisilla ja historiallisilla, rakenteellisilla tekijöillä.

title: Sinulla on idea. Meillä on kilpailu.
content:
Ylioppilaslehti käynnistää tiistaina 15.9.2026 avoimen ideakilpailun, jossa etsitään uusia tapoja tehdä opiskelijamediaa. Haemme rohkeita, yllättäviä ja toteuttamiskelpoisia ideoita, jotka voivat muuttaa tapaa, jolla opiskelijat löytävät sisältöjä, osallistuvat yhteisöihin ja rakentavat tulevaisuuden mediaa.  

Kilpailussa ei etsitä vain uusia juttuideoita. Voittava ehdotus voi liittyä yhtä hyvin sisältöihin, yhteisöllisyyteen, teknologiaan, liiketoimintamalleihin, tapahtumiin, jäsenyyksiin, tekoälyyn, digitaalisiin palveluihin tai johonkin, mitä emme ole vielä osanneet edes kuvitella.  

Ideakilpailu on avoin kaikille opiskelijamedian tulevaisuudesta kiinnostuneille. Osallistua voi yksin tai tiimin kanssa. Ideoita ei tarvitse keksiä tyhjästä: kaikki kilpailijat saavat käyttöönsä perehdytysmateriaalit, jotka tarjoavat tietoa Ylioppilaslehden nykytilasta, mediakentän muutoksista ja innovaatioiden kehittämisestä. Tavoitteena ei ole kerätä irrallisia ajatuksia, vaan löytää oikeasti perusteltuja ja vaikuttavia avauksia.

title: Why Pacific Island states should seek collective security for the region
content:
Many participants at the Pacific Islands Forum in Palau this week would like to talk about anything but great power rivalry: transnational crime, energy security, climate change, development finance, seabed minerals, transport links.

Instead, the meeting has been pulled toward the question that now shadows every Pacific regional gathering: what happens when the world’s great powers decide your part of the world is strategically important?

The answer does not have to involve choosing between them. For the Pacific’s small states, a more useful approach could be to seek shelter collectively.

Shelter theory was developed to explain a basic problem of small-state politics: countries with limited military, economic and diplomatic resources cannot provide everything they need for themselves.

They can instead choose to get collective protection and support from international and regional institutions or a larger power.

In the Pacific, sheltering together is becoming painfully urgent.

In June this year, a Chinese Liberation Army (PLA) submarine fired a long-range nuclear-capable ballistic missile with a dummy warhead into waters near Tuvalu.

title: Ilmastokriisi testaa turvallisuuskäsitystä – turvallisuus ei ole vain puolustusta
content:
Eurooppa varustautuu huomiseen, mutta kestääkö se tulevaisuuden, kun varustautuminen ja hyvinvointi ovat saman kolikon kaksi puolta?

Euroopan unioni elää voimakasta muodonmuutosta. Puolustusbudjetit kasvavat, omaa puolustusteollisuutta vahvistetaan ja Ukrainan tuki jatkuu, kuten asiaan kuuluu. Kova turvallisuus on noussut historiallisella tavalla keskiöön.

Samaan aikaan EU:ssa on kaikki syy arvioida kriittisesti ymmärrämmeko, miten ympäristö- ja ilmastokriisien tulisi laajentaa turvallisuuskäsitystämme lyhyen aikavälin puolustuksesta myös pitkän aikavälin kestävyyteen.

TÄNÄ kesänä on saatu esimakua tulevasta. Keski- ja Itä-Euroopassa on rikottu lämpöennätyksiä, esimerkiksi Slovakiassa 42 astetta. Helle ja kuivuus ovat ruokkineet maastopaloja, koetelleet ihmisten terveyttä ja painaneet suurten jokien vedenpintoja ennätyksellisen alas.

Puolassa kaksi hiilivoimalaa suljettiin, koska Veikselissä ei ollut riittävästi vettä niiden jäähdyttämiseen. Unkarissa Romaniassa ydinvoimaloiden tuotantoa rajoitettiin niin ikään kuivuuden johdosta.

Suomessa pohditaan eurooppalaiseen raideleveyteen siirtymistä, muualla sitä, kestävätkö raiteet tulevaisuuden ilmastoa.

title: Kiinan nousu ja aasianismin uusi tuleminen
content:
Itäisen Aasian yhteistyöpyrkimyksillä taloudessa ja turvallisuudessa on yli 150-vuotinen historia. Maailmanpolitiikan murros saattaa syventää yhteistyötä yli alueen suurvaltapoliittisen vastakkainasettelun.

Aasianismi tai pan-aasianismi on yksi 1800-luvun lopulla syntyneistä alueellisista pan-ismeistä. Sillä oli paljon kannattajia aina toiseen maailmansotaan asti, jolloin se hävisi muodista aasialaisessa politiikassa. Kiinan alueellisen nousun myötä aasianismi on kuitenkin tekemässä paluuta itäisen Aasian politiikkaan.

Aasianismin kannattajat uskoivat Aasian ja aasialaisten ykseyteen ja ajoivat aasialaisten valtioiden liittoa tai ainakin yhteistyötä länsimaiden kolonialismia vastaan. Aasialaisten nähtiin eroavan länsimaisista yhteisen henkisemmän kulttuurin, tai ainakin uskonnollisten ja filosofisten lähtökohtien, rodun ja joskus jopa teenjuonnin kautta. Aasianismin ydin ja käyttövoima oli kuitenkin länsimaiden kolonialismin vastustaminen.

title: Ihmisten suhdetta veteen voidaan ymmärtää veden tajun käsitteen kautta
content:
Vettä ei tulisi nähdä vain sääntelyn, ohjaamisen tai kontrollin kohteena, vaan kumppanina, jonka kanssa toimitaan muuttuvissa olosuhteissa vastavuoroisessa ja huoltapitävässä suhteessa. Näin tutkimusprofessori Katriina Soini tiivistää vetämänsä Veden taju -hankkeen keskeisen ajatuksen.

Luonnonvarakeskuksen, Suomen ympäristökeskuksen, Itä-Suomen yliopiston ja Aalto-yliopiston yhteisessä tutkimushankkeessa lähdettiin siitä ajatuksesta, että ihmisillä on tiedostamaton, vesisuhdettamme taustalla ohjaava veden taju. Hankkeessa etsittiin keinoja tehdä tästä tajusta näkyvää eri tilanteissa ja eri toimijoiden kanssa.

"Veden taju muodostuu vettä koskevasta ymmärryksestä, aisti- ja tunnekokemuksista sekä toiminnasta veden parissa", kuvailee Soini Luonnonvarakeskuksen tiedotteessa.

Tutkimuksen mukaan ihmiset rakentavat suhdettaan veteen eri tavoin: osaa ohjaa tieto ja ongelmanratkaisu, toisia muuttuvien tilanteiden herättämät tunteet, ja jotkut kuvaavat vesisuhdettaan ennen kaikkea käytäntöjen kautta.

title: Analysis: China’s CO2 emissions fall in Q2 2026 due to plummeting oil use
content:
China’s carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions fell by 1% in the second quarter of 2026, as oil consumption plummeted amid the strait of Hormuz crisis.

The country’s use of oil fell by 9% overall and by 16% for transport, after the disruptions to supply from the Gulf through the strait.

Lauri Myllyvirta, lead analyst at the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air

China’s total CO2 emissions fell despite a continued rebound in coal-fired power generation.

This is the first time that reductions in oil consumption have been responsible for a fall in CO2 emissions overall – in all previous cases, coal consumption has been the main driver.

Other key findings for the second quarter of 2026 include:

  • Electric vehicles (EVs) and public transport have become key factors in China’s oil demand, enabling transportation levels to increase even as fuel use fell sharply.
  • The effect of EVs on oil consumption was almost twice as large as would be expected based on the increase in the number of EVs on the road alone, as the usage of existing EVs surged.
  • Oil consumption displaced by EVs in China in the first half of 2026 exceeded the UK’s total oil consumption over a six-month period.

title: Fighting AI with AI: The US’s New Cyber Rules of Engagement
content:
It’s an important step in cyber policy. A new White House Memorandum on transnational cyber-enabled crime will allow vetted US companies to conduct specified cyber-surveillance against foreign criminal organizations. Every operation will require written government approval. 

The arrangement recognizes a structural reality: the private sector owns and operates much of the digital infrastructure and cutting-edge technology relevant to national security. It would be inefficient and uneconomic for governments to replicate these capabilities, originally built for the civilian economy. The memorandum points to a useful principle: private capabilities can be mobilized while authority and accountability remain public. 

Public-private cooperation in cybersecurity is not new. Governments have long relied on telecom companies and cloud providers for technical support. But traditionally, the private company controlled the infrastructure under attack, not the attacker itself.

title: Trust the evidence… especially when you obtain it through FOI
content:
Many of us may have wanted to put the Covid pandemic out of our minds once it passed — but those with more medical and scientific understanding would be justified in exploring a little more deeply into how well the UK government and our NHS services handled it. What can we see from the facts and figures around lockdowns, mortality rates and even the efficacy of testing?

One ideal tool for this type of enquiry is Freedom of Information — the right to ask public authorities for recorded information. And the Trust The Evidence project, run by Tom Jefferson and Carl Heneghan, has made very good use of that, thanks to WhatDoTheyKnow. 

Their approach? Small, focused FOI requests lodged via WhatDoTheyKnow (and therefore accessible for everyone to see), followed by deeper analysis and articles both in the media and on their own SubStack, which is supported by an engaged audience.

We asked Tom and Carl to tell us a bit more about how they’ve used FOI and what they have discovered about the UK’s response to the pandemic, as well as other pressing health matters. First of all, how have they come to be working together?

title: Investigating Inside Conflict Zones and Areas Controlled by Armed Groups: Lessons from Africa
content:
For investigative journalists in Africa, getting into an area controlled by armed groups may not be the most dangerous part of an assignment. The real challenge is figuring out how to report safely when armed groups control territory, access is restricted, information is unreliable, and the people who speak to you may face reprisals.

Journalists working in these environments make difficult decisions at every stage of an investigation: when it is safe to travel, whom to trust, how to reach sources, how to verify claims, and when to abandon a reporting plan.

Sometimes, staying away from the most dangerous areas and finding other ways to gather evidence becomes the safest option. According to Reporters Without Borders, more than 50 media professionals have been killed in Somalia since 2010, making it one of Africa’s most dangerous countries for journalists. In Mali, insecurity and political instability have restricted journalists’ access to information, while Ethiopia’s conflicts have raised fears of reprisals against journalists. In northern Nigeria, journalists encounter difficulties reporting on terrorist groups, bandits, and other armed actors involved in killings and abductions.

title: 1Lib1Ref 2026 Campaign in Nigeria

The campaign aimed to improve the quality, reliability, and verifiability of Wikipedia by encouraging librarians, Wikimedians, and knowledge enthusiasts across Nigeria to add missing citations to Wikipedia articles.This year’s campaign combined a nationwide editing contest with community-led edit-a-thons, complemented by virtual and in-person training sessions that equipped both new and experienced contributors with the skills needed to make impactful contributions.

Virtual Office Hour

A virtual office hour was held on 13 June 2026 to onboard new participants, provide editing guidance, and respond to questions about the campaign. The interactive session helped participants understand how to identify citation gaps and contribute effectively to Wikipedia.

Pelarbedömningen är en omfattande granskningsprocess som genomförs av en extern bedömare på uppdrag av Europeiska kommissionen i syfte att säkerställa att den organisation som ansöker följer EU:s strikta standarder för ekonomiförvaltning, riskhantering och intern kontroll.

Bedömningen omfattar bland annat intern kontroll, bokföring, upphandlingsprocesser samt principer för ansvarstagande. I Finland finns sedan tidigare endast fem organisationer som har genomgått pelarbedömning.

Den godkända pelarbedömningen är ett bevis på förmågan att förvalta omfattande internationella projekt på ett effektivt och ansvarsfullt sätt samt att skydda EU:s intressen. Detta är också ett erkännande av GTK:s konsekventa utvecklingsarbete. Europeiska unionen kan i framtiden bevilja EU-finansiering direkt till GTK för förvaltning utan ett separat konkurrensutsatt anbudsförfarande.

title: Euroopan tutkimusneuvoston huippurahoitus viidelle Helsingin yliopistossa
content:
Five University of Helsinki researchers have been awarded Starting Grants by the European Research Council (ERC). The €1.5-million grants are awarded to talented early-career researchers who have already conducted outstanding research and show potential to become research leaders.

Diabetes is a growing global health concern that requires novel therapies. One potential therapy is based on pancreatic islets produced from stem cells, but the resulting insulin-producing beta cells remain immature for the time being.

Assistant professor (Faculty of Medicine) ERC-funded research project uses genome engineering to enhance the maturation and resilience of these cells.

The project can help develop increasingly effective and personalised therapies for diabetes. At the same time, it can improve patients’ quality of life and reduce healthcare costs generated by diseases associated with diabetes. The project will also advance our knowledge of the development of cell replacement and gene editing therapies for other diseases.

title: Watch the Completely Unsafe, Vertigo-Inducing Footage of Workers Building New York’s Iconic Skyscrapers
content:
Would anyone in their right mind sign up for a job that had a high risk of mortality/disability? Or a job where red hot metal is being hurled directly at your face? Back in the 1920s this was the lot of the men who built New York’s skyline, the men who constructed the Chrysler Building and the Empire State, giant phallic symbols of America’s burgeoning wealth and power.

In this short clip (remastered and quite decently colorized) from the Smithsonian Channel, we get a brief glimpse of the perils encountered daily on the building site. Nicknamed “roughnecks,” the narrator points out that they work without harnesses, safety ropes, or hard hats. Red hot rivets are thrown at men on the metal beams higher up and they are meant to catch them with what looks like a tin funnel. You can see the thinnest of ropes used to lift the now-iconic stainless steel art-deco eagles into place by men wearing felt hats and no gloves.

The workers came from Europe, many who had trained on ships. Some came from Montreal’s Kahnawake reservation. The latter, known as Iron Walkers, were Mohawk, known for working fearlessly at great heights.

title: Judge Rules DOD Unlawfully Retaliated Against Anthropic
content: A federal judge has sided with Anthropic on its claims that the Department of Defense illegally retaliated against Anthropic’s protected speech by labeling the AI company a “supply chain risk.” The judge found that designation, intended to penalize Anthropic for telling the U.S. military it would not allow their technology to be used for mass surveillance of U.S. persons, “constituted unlawful retaliation in violation of the First Amendment.” EFF joined a coalition of organizations in filing multiple amicus briefs (here, here) arguing that the Pentagon had trampled on Anthropics First Amendment rights. We agree with the court’s decision and applaud the judge for slapping down such an obvious act of illegal and unconstitutional retribution by the Pentagon—even as the court left open the broader question of whether a company’s choices about how its technology may be used are protected speech in their own right.

title: TikTok ban divides European Commission
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Commission’s refusal to get on TikTok is facing pushback inside its Berlaymont HQ, with some officials arguing the EU is making a strategic mistake by staying off a platform used by around 200 million Europeans.

The question of whether the executive should establish a presence on Chinese-owned TikTok has come up in high-level meetings, with at least one commissioner arguing for a rethink, according to an official granted anonymity to discuss internal deliberations, as were others spoken to for this article.

The Commission banned TikTok from staff devices in 2023 over cybersecurity concerns. The ban also covers “personal devices enrolled in the Commission mobile device service,” a spokesperson for the institution said.

“We follow the evolution of the platform, in particular the status of developments regarding data protection and cybersecurity concerns,” the Commission said.

There is little sign the Commission’s policy is about to change. Dana Spinant, the Commission’s director-general for communications, opposes creating an official account, according to another official familiar with the discussions. Spinant did not respond to a request for comment.

title: Tunisia: Final judicial avenue to overturn convictions in unjust ‘conspiracy’ case
content:
Ahead of the final appeal hearing at Tunisia’s Court of Cassation on 3 September in the unjust “conspiracy case”, which is a chance to overturn the convictions of opposition figures jailed solely because of their peaceful political opposition, Sara Hashash, Deputy Regional Director for the Middle East and North Africa at Amnesty International said: 

“Tunisia’s authorities must seize this opportunity to rectify a travesty of justice that has upturned the lives of 34 prominent opposition figures, human rights defenders and lawyers who were convicted on unfounded charges in a mass trial marred by due process violations. These defendants were targeted with politically motivated charges and should have never been imprisoned in the first place. Many of them have been languishing in jail with deteriorating health problems, with recent successive heatwaves further worsening detention conditions inside poorly ventilated cells. 

It is time to put an end to this pattern of instrumentalizing the justice system to target dissent. 

Sara Hashash, Amnesty International

title: Prisoner Executed in Shiraz’s Adelabad Prison
content:
According to HRANA, a prisoner was executed in Shiraz’s Adelabad Prison.

HRANA has confirmed the identity of the prisoner, who was hanged at dawn today, Wednesday, September 2, as Aziz Roshanayi.

According to information received by HRANA, Mr. Roshanayi had previously been arrested on a murder charge and was subsequently sentenced to death by a criminal court.

As of the time of this report, the prisoner’s execution has not been officially announced by prison officials or the relevant authorities.

According to HRA’s Annual Report, in 2025 at least 2,063 citizens, including 61 women and 2 juvenile offenders, were executed. Of these, the sentences of 11 individuals were carried out in public. During the same period, 172 other individuals were sentenced to death.

title: Tragedy at Pakistani Hospital Should Prompt Reform
content:
Fourteen newborns died in a fire on August 26 at one of Pakistan’s largest public hospitals, and their shattered families are asking how this could have happened.

The preliminary inquiry report found that the neonatal ward at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences in Islamabad, Pakistan’s capital, had no fire alarm or sprinkler system, and that emergency procedures were inadequate. The fire engulfed the nursery within two minutes. Even more troubling, the hospital had experienced another fire just seven weeks earlier, on July 6. That earlier inquiry had already identified problems with fire detection, alarms, evacuation preparedness, electrical inspections, and emergency response. But nothing was done.

While the inquiry is at a preliminary stage and does not establish individual responsibility, it makes it clear that the hospital was shockingly unprepared in the event of a fire.

title: Ukraine Presidential Chief Responds to Alleged Laundering Role
content:
The head of Ukraine’s presidential office, has said courts should determine the significance of recordings that have raised questions about his involvement in an alleged $3.3 million money-laundering scheme aimed at securing bail for a former minister detained in a sprawling energy sector corruption probe.

Authorities have not publicly named Kyrylo Budanov and he has not been charged but  court documents obtained by the Ukrainian news outlet hromadske appear to identify him participating in a conversation concerning the money laundering.

Responding to questions about the tapes, Budanov told hromadske that any determination regarding the recordings should be made by a judge. “Let the court figure out who appears where,” he said.

title: Several States Rejected This Private School Chain as a Charter. Now It’s Eligible for Texas’ Taxpayer-Funded Vouchers.
content:
The rejections piled up one after another as leaders of Alpha School, a growing network of private school campuses, tried to convince states that their artificial-intelligence-led teaching model belonged in publicly funded charter schools.

The Alpha system is centered on the idea that students can “crush academics,” like reading and math lessons, in just two hours a day. AI software teaches the lessons. The human teachers, referred to as guides, focus on motivation and emotional support. “School is broken, and we’re here to fix it,” Alpha’s “2 Hour Learning” tagline claims.

But over the last two years, officials in numerous states have questioned the model,  characterizing it as “untested” and ”experimental.” In North Carolina, one charter school board member feared two hours was “not nearly enough” to teach required subjects. A month earlier, in August 2024, an official in Utah worried that the school’s instructors may act more like “a life coach” than a teacher.

Even the largely conservative Texas State Board of Education, which had approved most charter applications over the last decade, rejected Alpha’s pitch last summer.

title: Mohamed Yahya
content:
Mohamed Yahya is Assistant Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Deputy Emergency Relief Coordinator, OCHA. He started his official duties on 1 September 2026.

Prior to this, he served as UN Resident Coordinator and Humanitarian Coordinator in Pakistan, leading one of the largest UN presences in Asia and the Pacific and coordinating the UN's response to the 2025 floods. 

He brings more than two decades of experience in humanitarian action, development, and peacebuilding, gained at headquarters, regional and field levels across Africa and South Asia. Before his appointment in Pakistan, he worked in Nigeria, where he led one of the largest country offices of the UN Development Programme (UNDP).

He previously coordinated UNDP's Africa Regional Programme, working with the African Union on conflict prevention and stabilization across the continent. Earlier in his career, he held positions with the UN and International Alert in West Africa and in Afghanistan.

Yahya holds a Master's degree in Conflict and Development and a Bachelor's in Politics and History from SOAS University of London and speaks Swahili, English and Somali.

title: Palaces and the Pope: the fascinating story of how Renaissance Rome was rebuilt
content:
Nearly 31% of Rome’s palaces were built between 1378 and 1599, after a century of economic stagnation. What were the origins of this striking urban revival? Drawing on a newly compiled dataset linking palace construction to the identity of their patrons, a study shows that Romans began building palaces only once they were confident the popes would not leave the Eternal City again.

Rome, in the 14th and 15th centuries, was in ruins. Contemporaries described it as a “cadaver”. A “great stable for sheep”. Artists depicted Rome as a widow, clad in black, pleading with passersby.

Then, in the late 15th century, came an economic revolution. A new era of palace-building dawned in Rome. A city that had been suffering from dereliction and decay transformed into a flourishing metropolis: of all historically significant palazzi erected in Rome from antiquity to the 21st century, 31% were built between 1378 and 1599.

How did Rome recover? What was the origin of its palace-building boom, nearly a century after the Renaissance had come to the rest of Italy?

title: Laivaliikenne saastuttaa, mutta sähköinen laivaliikenne voi olla kulman takana
content:
Laivaliikenne nähdään usein ekologisempana vaihtoehtona lentämiselle, mutta ongelmatonta se ei ole. Transport & Environment -järjestön (T&E) selvityksen mukaan monissa Euroopan satama­kaupungeissa lauttaliikenne tuottaa enemmän hiilidioksidipäästöjä kuin samojen kaupunkien henkilöautot.

Selvityksestä nousee esiin muitakin mielenkiintoisia tietoja laivaliikenteen saastuttavuudesta.

Eniten saastuttava reitti Euroopassa on Helsinki–Travemünde. Satamista eniten hiilidioksidipäästöjä tulee Barcelonasta. Eniten rikin oksideja tulee Dublinin satamasta.

Tutkimuksessa analysoitiin 1 043 laivan päästöjä vuonna 2023. Niiden yhteenlasketut hiilidioksidipäästöt olivat 13,4 miljoonaa tonnia, mikä vastaa noin 6,6 miljoonan auton päästöjä.

Eurooppalaislaivojen keski-ikä on 26 vuotta. Suurin osa kulkee polttomoottorilla ja dieselillä. Pieni osa käyttää myös nesteytettyä maakaasua, kokonaan sähköisiä on vain kaksi prosenttia.

Laivoille on jo olemassa erilaisia päästörajoituksia, mutta T&E:n mukaan laivaliikenteen sähköistäminen olisi hyvä ratkaisu. 60 prosenttia laivoista voitaisiin sähköistää vuoteen 2035 mennessä. Yli puolet myös kulkisi sen jälkeen halvemmalla.

title: Despite losing everything, communities along the Nepal-Tibet border are helping each other rebuild
content:
Hearts across the globe are aching for communities along the Nepal-Tibet border.

Last Wednesday, a catastrophic flash flood ripped apart whole villages and swept away dozens of vital bridges and roads. It has claimed the lives of more than 1000 people, as authorities race to find thousands more who are unaccounted for and free hundreds of trapped hydropower tunnel workers.

In the wake of the flood, the world has rallied to support ongoing rescue and humanitarian efforts. But as with any disaster, shifting from rescue to recovery will be far from straightforward. Soniya, co-author of this article and a Nepali national, experienced this firsthand while providing humanitarian assistance to communities rocked by the deadly 2015 Nepal earthquake.

Our research shows local communities are critical to ensuring disaster-hit regions can recover and rebuild.

Read more: Satellite images show how the Nepal flood disaster unfolded

It is difficult to comprehend the scale and severity of the Nepal-Tibet floods.

Families around the world are grieving, with many still wondering whether their loved ones are even alive.
snippet: Hearts across the globe are aching for communities along the Nepal-Tibet border.
creator: Soniya Rijal, Postdoctoral Research Associate in organising in and around exterme events, University of Sydney

title: EU:n ilmastokomissaari: Komissio ei ole heikentämässä päästökauppajärjestelmää
content:
EU:n ilmastokomissaari Wopke Hoekstra kiistää syytökset siitä, että EU-komissio olisi heikentämässä unionin päästökauppajärjestelmää.

Komissio esitteli heinäkuussa ehdotuksensa unionin päästökauppajärjestelmän uudistamiseksi ja se sai kriittisen vastaanoton etenkin ympäristöjärjestöiltä.

Esimerkiksi WWF moitti komission ehdotusta päästökauppajärjestelmän vesittämisestä. WWF:n mukaan päästökauppajärjestelmä on ollut EU:n ilmastopolitiikan menestystarina, kun päästökaupan piiriin kuuluvien teollisuuslaitosten päästöt ovat laskeneet puoleen vuodesta 2005 vuoteen 2024.

Hoekstran mukaan komissio haluaa päinvastoin vahvistaa ja tehostaa päästökauppajärjestelmää ja tehdä siitä käytännönläheisemmän.

Hollantilaiskomissaarin mukaan komissio ehdottaa tavoitetason nostamista muun muassa merenkulussa ja ilmailussa.

- Jos vertaamme vuosia 2020-2030 tämän ehdotukseen vuosiin 2030-2040, tavoitteemme ovat aiempaa kunnianhimoisempia, Hoekstra sanoi Helsingissä järjestetyssä tiedotustilaisuudessa.

HOEKSTRAN mukaan komission ehdotuksessa yrityksiltä edellytetään, että ne, jotka saavat ilmaisia ​​päästöoikeuksia, tekevät todellisia investointeja hiilidioksidipäästöjen vähentämiseksi Euroopassa.

title: Suomen valtioenemmistöisen Neovan turvekiista kärjistyi Ruotsissa – suomalaisaktivistia uhkaa maahantulokielto
content:
Johanna Kohvakka

Länsi-Ruotsissa sijaitsevasta Grimsåsin suosta on tullut yksi Ruotsin näkyvimmistä turpeennostoon liittyvistä ympäristökiistoista. Vastakkain ovat suomalainen turveyhtiö Neova, paikalliset turpeennoston vastustajat ja suoran toiminnan ympäristöliike Återställ Våtmarker (Ennallistetaan kosteikot).

Suomen valtio omistaa Neovasta 50,1 prosenttia. Yhtiö toimii turvetuotannossa Suomen lisäksi Ruotsissa ja Virossa, ja sen Kekkilä-BVB -liiketoiminta valmistaa turpeeseen pohjautuvia kasvualustoja.

Återställ Våtmarker on vastustanut turpeennostoa Grimsåsissa nyt kolmatta kesää. Voima-lehden elokuussa julkaiseman reportaasin mukaan tämän kesän leirille osallistui noin 60 ihmistä muun muassa Ruotsista, Suomesta, Puolasta, Belgiasta, Iso-Britanniasta ja Norjasta. Aktivistit ovat aiempina vuosina pysäyttäneet työkoneita ja tukkineet suoalueen ojia. Tänä kesänä he ovat myös kylväneet turpeennostoalueelle niittykasveja ja auringonkukkia.

Kiistan ytimessä on se, mihin tarkoitukseen Grimsåsin turvetta tosiasiassa nostetaan.

title: Europe’s Spies: Fighting as a Team
content:
Europe’s intelligence and security agencies don’t have the luxury of operating in a broadly calm world. Significant geopolitical pressure is being applied by the informal axis of Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea, while relations with the US have frayed.

That is bringing change. In recent weeks, Germany has approved a draft law allowing its agencies – the Bundesnachrichtendienst (BND) and Bundesamt für Verfassungsschutz (BfV) – to take a more active role in responding to Russia’s hybrid threats. Sweden, too, has taken steps to create a new civilian-led agency (the Sveriges utrikes underrättelsetjänst or UND), taking powers from the traditionally military service. 

Europe’s relationship with its traditional ally, the United States, is stretched and there have been reports that European agencies are withholding intelligence. Last year Erik Akerboom, Director General of the Netherlands’ AIVD agency, suggested his service was increasingly hesitant to share intelligence material with US counterparts, whilst the UK and other US allies suspended some sharing of intelligence over drug strikes in the Caribbean.

title: Wikipedia as an Educational Tool in Achachicala
content: It’s common to hear phrases like, “But that’s not serious—that’s from Wikipedia,” in educational communities or academic settings. Although virtually all of us have used Wikipedia at some point—often to begin a research project—we rarely acknowledge it or cite it in our bibliographies. We know that students use it to do their homework and that even artificial intelligence relies on it as one of its main sources of information, yet we still fail to fully recognize its value as an educational tool. Objectively speaking, however, it is a very powerful educational tool. That’s why, to me, recognizing that value is, at the very least, only fair.

title: Google defeats US justice department bid to force ad tech sale
content:
Judge declines to make Google sell AdX in win for firm against US antitrust enforcers’ attempts to break up big tech

Alphabet’s Google escaped a breakup of its advertising technology business on Wednesday, when a judge in Virginia ⁠rejected US antitrust enforcers’ attempt to force a sale of Google’s online advertising exchange.

While the ad exchange is a small part of Google’s business, the ruling is the second powerful ⁠symbolic victory against the US Department ⁠of Justice in ​its efforts to force Google to sell assets to address illegal monopolies.

title: Geologian tutkimuskeskus läpäisi EU:n pilariarvioinnin ensimmäisenä suomalaisena tutkimuslaitoksena ja eurooppalaisena geoalan toimijana
content:
Pilariarviointi on ulkoisen arvioitsijan Euroopan komissiolle suorittama perusteellinen arviointiprosessi, jonka tarkoituksena on varmistaa, että pilariarviointia hakeva organisaatio noudattaa EU:n varainhallinnan, riskienhallinnan ja valvonnan tiukkoja standardeja.

Arviointi kattaa muun muassa sisäisen valvonnan, kirjanpidon, hankintaprosessien sekä vastuullisuuden periaatteiden läpikäynnin. Suomessa on ennestään vain viisi pilariarvioitua organisaatiota.

Hyväksytty pilariarviointi on osoitus kyvystä hallinnoida laajoja kansainvälisiä hankkeita tehokkaasti, vastuullisesti ja suojaten EU:n etuja. Tämä on tunnustus myös GTK:n johdonmukaiselle kehittämistyölle. Euroopan Unioni voi jatkossa myöntää EU-rahoitusta suoraan GTK:n hallinnoitavaksi ilman erillistä kilpailutusta.

”Hakemuksemme hyväksyminen avaa uusia mahdollisuuksia johtaa suuria EU-rahoitteisia kansainvälisiä ohjelmia EU:n kumppanuusmaissa. Se on luottamuksen osoitus, ja vahvistaa entisestään Suomen roolia kansainvälisessä yhteistyössä eurooppalaisena tutkimusorganisaationa”, sanoo Geologian tutkimuskeskuksen pääjohtaja Saku Vuori.

title: Project MUSE - The Data Rescue Project: A Crowdsourced Effort to Preserve At-Risk US Federal Data
content: Abstract: The US federal government is the world's largest data publisher. Since Trump's second inauguration, these data are threatened because their scope contravenes regime ideology and the offices that maintain these datasets no longer have adequate staff to preserve and provide access to the data. The Data Rescue Project was launched in 2025 as a community response to this crisis. We organized volunteers to work on data rescues, focusing especially on social data to fill an identified gap in other rescue efforts and emphasizing curation of the datasets for long-term data preservation. Through community-building, we became a coordinating body for the data rescue movement, streamlining communication and preventing duplication of effort in the US and internationally. In this article, we use the Data Rescue Project as a case study on building coalitions to push back against the destruction of digital information. Moreover, the US is not unique in its need for these efforts. The need to rapidly capture data from natural disasters, war zones, or unforeseen crises is a component of the digital preservation ecosystem that has been undercovered in the existing literature. content:

title: The EU is ready to bet billions on data centers. Not all countries want in.
content:
BRUSSELS — The global frenzy to build massive AI data centers is coming to Europe. Just not all of Europe.

Two-thirds of European Union governments have pledged money to back an EU plan to create seven large AI compute hubs, the bloc’s most significant industrial policy push in the global race for artificial intelligence infrastructure. But nine countries have refrained from committing funds at a time when national budgets are already stretched.

The United States has so far led the global race to provide enough compute power to feed the artificial intelligence boom, with tech giants like OpenAI, Anthropic and Elon Musk’s xAI putting in private investment through projects like Stargate and Colossus, and building out their lead in expanding data centers.

In Europe, Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced a plan last year to spend EU funding to establish seven so-called gigafactories — three larger and four smaller ones — across the EU, meant to help researchers and startups train very large AI models.
snippet: BRUSSELS — The global frenzy to build massive AI data centers is coming to Europe. Just not all of Europe.

title: EU: ‘Return hub’ plans in Rwanda and Uganda risk becoming ‘cruel black holes’ for human rights
content:
Ahead of the 4 September meeting between Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece and the Netherlands to discuss progress on plans to deport people to so-called “return hubs” in countries outside Europe where they may never have set foot, likely be to centres or facilities funded by EU member states, Eve Geddie, Director of the European Institutions Office of Amnesty International, said:

“By their very design, and wherever they may be located, ‘return hubs’ carry a risk of grave human rights violations, including arbitrary detention, torture and ill-treatment, and forced onward returns to countries of origin. There is a real danger that these locations will, in practice, become cruel black holes for human rights to outsource or offshore detention and deportation. Any responsible government should reject these plans outright.

“We are particularly alarmed that discussions are reportedly zeroing in on two countries with appalling human rights records: Uganda and Rwanda – despite ongoing conflict and political instability in the Great Lakes Region.
snippet: Ahead of the 4 September meeting between Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece and the Netherlands to discuss progress on plans to deport people to so-called “return hubs” in countries outside Europe

title: Ali-Asghar Peyghambari, Prisoner Sentenced to Death, Held in Ghezel Hesar Prison
content:
According to HRANA, Ali-Asghar Peyghambari, 26, who was arrested during the nationwide protests of January 2026, is currently imprisoned in Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj.

According to information received by HRANA, Peyghambari is currently being held in Ward 37 of Unit 3 at the prison. He was previously sentenced to death by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court on charges of “operational and security-related actions against the regime” and “encouraging individuals to participate in protests,” under the Law on Intensifying Punishment for Espionage and Cooperation with Israel. His sentence was recently upheld by Branch 9 of the Supreme Court.

Payam Derafshan, one of Peyghambari’s attorneys, previously stated that his client had no organizational or other ties to “hostile groups” and that, according to the defense presented in court, the only action attributed to him was attending one of the protests. He also announced that a request for a retrial and a stay of execution had been prepared.

Ali-Asghar (Alireza) Peyghambari was arrested by security forces on January 9, 2026, amid the nationwide protests. He was released on bail in March of the same year.

title: Sweden: Most Parties Back Stronger Action on Israel
content:
(Stockholm) – A majority of Swedish parliamentary parties support significantly stronger measures to curb Israeli government abuses in the Occupied Palestinian Territory than current policies suggest, six civil society organizations said today.

The groups released a survey ahead of the September 13, 2026 general election. Seven of the eight parties in the Riksdag, Sweden’s parliament, responded to the survey, a joint initiative by Act Church of Sweden, Amnesty International Sweden, Diakonia, Human Rights Watch, Swedish Fellowship of Reconciliation, and the Swedish Peace and Arbitration Society, who have now published the results.

“This survey provides important information from the Swedish parliamentary parties on the steps Sweden needs to take to address grave human rights concerns with the Israeli government,” said Christina Abdulahad, advocacy officer at Human Rights Watch. “It is crucial for Sweden’s next government, whatever its composition, to bring Swedish policy in line with its international legal obligations.”

title: Texas Police Used AI to Write Report About Using Flock to Search for Woman Who Had Abortion
content:
The Texas sheriff’s office that used Flock to search more than 80,000 cameras nationwide for a woman who had a self-administered abortion used Axon’s Draft One AI tool to help write a police report about the incident, documents shared with 404 Media show. The tool was used in part to summarize a discussion of “the legal implications of the situation.”

404 Media first reported on the incident in May 2025 in which the Johnson County Sheriff’s Office in Texas searched Flock’s nationwide network for the whereabouts of a woman who self-administered an abortion, highlighting the threat of this AI-powered surveillance system being used to criminalize or track women seeking reproductive healthcare. The use of both Flock and Axon’s Draft One, which uses audio from body camera footage to automatically draft police reports using artificial intelligence, shows how quickly police departments have come to use AI surveillance tools even in critically sensitive cases. 

“I acknowledge this report was generated using Draft One by Axon,” a section of the report reads.

title: Dutch Police Arrest 34 Following Drug-related Shootout
content:
Dutch authorities arrested 34 people Wednesday at various locations across the country following a deadly shootout in a Dutch village, reportedly linked to a notorious drug lord, public broadcaster NOS reported.

The incident unfolded around 4:00 a.m. Tuesday when dozens of masked men, several armed with heavy firearms, disembarked from two vans in Overasselt, near the German border. The group approached a farm belonging to a family allegedly involved in drug trafficking and opened fire on a car. The 51-year-old man inside the vehicle was killed, police told a press conference. The masked men also fired at two police officers, leaving one with life-threatening injuries.

title: Hurricane Helene Killed His Wife and Destroyed His Mobile Home. New Tenants Are Now Renting the Same Flood-Prone Land.
content:
Dave Masters could no longer ignore the storm as trees cracked and the swollen river roared. It was dark outside, but through the window he could see his father’s house, usually 100 feet away from the Pigeon River, was surrounded by water. Masters, tall and slender, forded the frigid waist-deep water to wake up his father and convince the 63-year-old to evacuate.

From the son’s trailer on the hillside, the two watched the water rise as Hurricane Frances wreaked havoc on Western North Carolina in early September 2004. Within an hour, his father’s home floated up like a bobber on a fishing line and then sailed down the middle of the road before veering into a telephone pole and cracking in half. The two pieces finally stopped when they got caught under a bridge downstream.

Just 10 days later, Hurricane Ivan dumped more rain in an unprecedented double whammy for the mountainous region far from the coast. Haywood County realized it needed to prevent further harm. It condemned several neighboring mobile homes along with a wood-frame house across the river.

title: Childhood sleep apnoea: when snoring is more than a noisy night
content:
A child who snores loudly every night might seem like a funny sight. But if that snoring accompanies repeated narrowing or blockage of the airway, the effects can reach far beyond a noisy night.

Obstructive sleep apnoea is often associated with adults who snore and struggle to stay awake during the day. Children can develop it too. Its prevalence is difficult to pin down: a 2024 systematic review of 30 studies found that recent estimates in preschool children ranged from 12.8% to 20.4%, but definitions and testing methods varied considerably. Only two population studies used a full overnight sleep study, so the true figure remains uncertain.

In children, habitual loud snoring is an important warning sign. Parents may also notice mouth breathing, restless sleep, pauses followed by gasps or snorts, or the chest and abdomen working hard to draw breath. Not every child who snores has sleep apnoea, however, and symptoms alone cannot confirm it.

title: A landmark UN report says the world will overshoot the 1.5°C climate target. What happens now?
content:
For over a decade, the world has been trying to limit global warming to 1.5°C.

That’s no longer possible, according to a new United Nations report. We will likely pass 1.5°C in 2030. That’s not good news for anyone, least of all Australia’s Pacific Island neighbours who face rapidly rising seas.

In response to the report, Palau’s President Surangel Whipps Jr said:

It is hard to overstate the depth of emotion for those of us living on the frontline after having fought so hard to put the 1.5 degree limit at the heart of the Paris Agreement […] calls for greater ambition are no longer enough — we need to see an urgent and unprecedented increase in political will and investment in a climate safe future

title: Tutkija Venäjän hybriditoiminnasta Saksassa: ”Ei tämä ole sotaa, mutta ei ihan rauhaakaan”
content:
Venäjän harmaan alueen toiminta eli niin sanottu hybriditoiminta Euroopassa on lisääntynyt.

Taustalla on Venäjän näkemys, että sen Ukrainassa käymä sota on laajempi konflikti Venäjän ja lännen välillä. Ulkopoliittisen instituutin vanhempi tutkija Matti Pesu sanoo, että Venäjä pyrkii konkreettisesti heikentämään Ukrainan länneltä saamaa tukea esimerkiksi tuhopolttamalla asevarastoja, häiritsemällä junaliikennettä tai tekemällä kyberiskuja.

Ukraina saa länneltä taloudellista ja sotilaallista apua, mikä on sille sodassa suuri voimareservi.

- Sellainen reservi, mikä Venäjältä itseltään puuttuu. Koska näistä maista valtaosa on Naton jäseniä, se on sellainen alue, jossa Venäjä ei sotilaallisesti kykene tai halua toimia, koska siinä on liian iso riski, sanoo Pesu STT:lle.

Saksan hallitus ilmoitti tiistaina, että Venäjä on vastuussa tapauksesta, jossa räjähteillä lastattu drooni löytyi Leipzigin lentokentältä ukrainalaisen rahtikoneen läheltä elokuun alussa. Lentokentän läheltä löytyi myös toinen drooni, josta löytyi merkkejä räjähteistä.

Pesun mukaan isku olisi onnistuessaan vaikeuttanut Ukrainan saamaa tukea.

title: Wiki Loves Mingachevir: Turkic Wikimedians United in Azerbaijan
content:
From August 12 to 16, Mingachevir hosted Wikimedians from across the Turkic world. The five-day Wiki Loves Mingachevir camp brought together members of the Azerbaijani Wikimedia community and international participants to share their experiences, learn from each other, and work on Wikimedia projects together.

The camp was organized by the Azerbaijani Wikimedians User Group with the support of the Ministry of Youth and Sports of the Republic of Azerbaijan and sponsored by Azersun Holding. The event was held as part of the celebrations for Wikipedia’s 25th anniversary.

I was part of the organizing team together with A.Aida88 and NurAy. One of our main goals was to create an environment where participants could learn from one another and spend time together beyond their usual online interactions.

Throughout the camp, participants took part in workshops, community presentations, edit-a-thons, team activities, and discussions about the future of Wikimedia. With contributors from five countries working and spending time together, Mingachevir became a place for Wikimedia communities to connect beyond their usual online collaboration.

title: Grand Theft Auto VI is a phenomenon – but there is much more to the gaming world
content:
As Rockstar’s blockbuster prepares to dominate the headlines, it’s time for the mainstream media to stop treating video games as a novelty that needs explaining

Predictably, the Grand Theft Auto VI “extended look” which premiered on Netflix last week was a success for all involved. The 30-minute preview scorched to No 1 on the viewing chart and even brought the site down for a few minutes as millions of gamers tried to watch what was, effectively, a very long teaser trailer. According to data collated by Eurogamer, more than 9,000 Twitch streamers covered the show leading to 5,227,798 hours of viewing there alone. And this was just the beginning of what will surely be two months of escalating hype – and unprecedented media attention.
snippet: As Rockstar’s blockbuster prepares to dominate the headlines, it’s time for the mainstream media to stop treating video games as a novelty that needs explaining

title: Tietokirja kartoittaa koulukiusaamisen ja siihen puuttumisen historian Suomessa ja osoittaa, että ilmiöön tartuttiin vasta myöhään
content:
Ennakkotiedote. Embargo 22.9.2026.

Toimittaja ja palkittu tietokirjailija Tuomo Tamminen kuvaa kirjassaan Miksi emme auttaneet? Koulukiusaamiseen puuttumisen liian lyhyt historia, kuinka koulukiusaaminen ilmiönä tunnistettiin ja nimettiin Suomessa. Ulossulkemista ja väkivaltaa on esiintynyt aina, mutta siihen kiinnitettiin kunnolla huomiota vasta 1990-luvulla.

Kiusaaminen esitetään usein nykypäivän ilmiönä, vaikka sitä on ollut suomalaisissa kouluissa aikaan katsomatta. Koulukiusaamisen sijaan puhuttiin kuitenkin esimerkiksi toverisorrosta, mobbaamisesta tai sakinhivutuksesta – tai tavallisemmin oltiin kokonaan puhumatta.

Miksi emme auttaneet? -teoksessa Tuomo Tamminen kartoittaa ensimmäistä kertaa koulukiusaamisen ja siihen puuttumisen historian Suomessa. Muistitietoon, lehtikirjoitteluun, tutkijoiden, opettajien ja poliitikoiden haastatteluihin sekä muuhun tutkimukseen pohjautuen Tamminen osoittaa, että ulossulkeminen ja väkivalta ovat toistuneet koulumaailmassa vuosikymmenestä toiseen. Esille nousevat esimerkiksi evakkolasten kohtelu, huorittelu, homottelu ja seksuaalinen ahdistelu sekä vähintään 1960-luvulle vallinnut karaisemiseen tähtäävä kasvatusajattelu.

title: IU’s Luddy School digitizes Revolutionary War artifacts
content: "The 3-D digitization will take pictures all around the object and process them, using a photogrammetric procedure which identifies common features in the different images. The process orients the images in space and then performs what’s called the calibration of the camera, Guidi said. Once these steps are completed, image matching will automatically generate a dense cloud of 3-D points. This leads to generating the mesh, which is the model, the shape of the object, and its texture, he said. “You have to take several photographs around the object, and then you merge them and you process them in such a way…(that) gives you a digital twin of the physical object,” he said. “A digital twin means that also the size is totally the same, so it can be measured and analyzed, and this is very useful if you want to study something.” Possible challenges will be digitizing shiny or transparent objects because they are not compatible with the optical process used to generate the model. Guidi said they have dealt with this issue before in past projects and should be able to solve it this time. title: Namibia: Drought displaced Angolans face human rights abuses
content:
Angolan women and children displaced by drought into Namibia face serious human rights abuses arising from a lack of safe and legal migration pathways for people forced across borders by natural disasters, Amnesty International said in a new report. 

The report, “The Drier It Gets The Longer You Have To Walk, The Deeper You Have To Dig” – The Human Rights Impacts Of Drought-induced Displacement On Angolan Women & Children In Namibia, documents the devastating consequences of recurrent drought in southern Angola and the human rights impacts experienced by those displaced into Namibia, including persistent fear of arrest, detention and deportation, which in turn influences their daily decisions about whether to seek healthcare and other services.  

“Namibian authorities must establish a rights-based approach to migration, ensuring that people displaced by drought and other natural disasters can access basic rights, including registration and documentation.” Said Tigere Chagutah, Amnesty International’s Regional Director for East and Southern Africa.

title: Prisoner Executed in Babol Prison
content:
According to HRANA, a prisoner was executed in Babol Prison at dawn today, Wednesday, September 2. HRANA has identified the prisoner as Ali Mirrezaei, a local Mazandarani singer.

According to information received by HRANA, Mirrezaei was arrested in 2021 after a fight resulted in the death of one person and was charged with murder. He was subsequently sentenced to death by a criminal court.

Ali Mirrezaei had been taken to the gallows three months ago for the execution of his sentence. However, the victim’s family granted him a three-month reprieve, postponing the execution.

According to HRA’s Annual Report, in 2025 at least 2,063 citizens, including 61 women and 2 juvenile offenders, were executed. Of these, the sentences of 11 individuals were carried out in public. During the same period, 172 other individuals were sentenced to death.

title: Tunisia: Civil Society Under Siege
content:
(Beirut) – The Tunisian government has systematically cracked down on civil society groups and their members since 2024, all but shutting down the vibrant civic space that emerged after the 2011 revolution, Human Rights Watch said in a report released today. The authorities should immediately end their crackdown on civil society and allow space for civic groups to operate fully and freely.

The 49-page report, “‘We Are Living on Borrowed Time’: Repression of Civil Society in Tunisia” documents the Tunisian authorities’ escalating repression of local and international civil society groups, workers, members, and affiliates through the weaponization of abusive prosecutions, arbitrary arrests, detention, financial and criminal investigations, mass suspensions, and threats of dissolution. 

“Civil society groups in Tunisia play a key role in holding power to account, delivering essential services, and advocating for people’s human rights,” said Bassam Khawaja, deputy Middle East and North Africa director at Human Rights Watch. “It is clear that the authorities are abusing every tool at their disposal to close the space for civil society in Tunisia and shut these organizations down.”
