title: Puolukkasato kypsyi tavanomaista paremmin – poimintakausi jatkuu pitkälle syksyyn
content:
Pressmeddelandet finns tillgängligt på svenska på Naturresursinstitutets webbplats

Suomalaiset ovat saaneet nauttia kuluvana marjakautena hyvästä mustikkasadosta. Myös puolukasta on tiedossa hyvä sato, selviää Luonnonvarakeskuksen (Luke) loppukesän satoennusteesta.

Puolukan pölytys onnistui pääosin keskimääräisesti tai keskimääräistä paremmin. Parhaiten pölytys onnistui maan etelä- ja keskiosissa Pohjois-Savon ja Keski-Pohjanmaan korkeudelle asti. Pohjois-Suomessa pölytys oli pääosin keskimääräistä.

Kesä on ollut paikoin hyvin sateinen, mutta sateisuus ei ole heikentänyt puolukkasatoa. Suurimmassa osassa maata puolukan marjat ovat kypsyneet tavanomaista paremmin. Yli 80 prosenttia raaoista puolukoista kypsyi tai on kypsymässä poimintakelpoisiksi marjoiksi.

Hyvin onnistunut pölytys ja marjojen tavallista parempi kypsyminen ennakoi monin paikoin hyvää puolukkasatoa. Parhaat poimintapaikat löytyvät valoisilta ja melko avoimilta kuivahkoilta kankailta, kuten harvahkoista männiköistä. Myös metsänuudistusalat voivat olla hyviä marja-apajia.

title: “The UK is yet to have a national reckoning around its role in colonialism”
content:
Lavinya Stennett, 29, is founder and CEO of The Black Curriculum, an educational tool that enables young people across the UK – and beyond – to learn about the history of colonialism.

Here, she shares what inspired the idea, why reparatory justice matters and the impact her organization is having on young people…


In 2016, I received my A Level results. I didn’t get my first-choice university, so went through clearing [how universities and colleges fill any places they still have on their courses]. I received a place at SOAS to do African Studies. I didn’t know much about the university, but my mum insisted I go.

The course changed my life. Prior to my degree, I hadn’t been able to access any information around African history that was empowering or wasn’t just focused on enslavement.

I started learning from African lecturers and it was such a grounding experience. I received a scholarship to go to Aotearoa New Zealand, where I learned a lot about Māori land law, as well as issues around the colonization and theft of land, and it just put everything into context.

The main aim of  The Black Curriculum is to empower all students with a sense of identity and belonging.

Lavinya Stennett

title: Sri Lanka: Tepid Progress on Justice for Past Abuses
content:
(Geneva, September 1, 2026) – The Sri Lankan government’s prosecution of past grave abuses has lagged, raising concerns for future progress, Human Rights Watch said in a report released today. United Nations officials and UN member countries at the Human Rights Council should call on the government led by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to show greater determination to address emblematic rights cases and cooperate with international accountability efforts.

The 49-page report, “‘Not Genuine with Justice’: Sri Lanka’s Lack of Will to Prosecute Past Abuses,” provides an overview of domestic justice efforts in seven prominent cases of grave abuses in which the Dissanayake government has made a measure of progress since taking office in 2024. Human Rights Watch found that many emblematic cases, including a massacre of aid workers, the targeting of journalists, and enforced disappearances of academics and others, remain stalled, while families of victims and human rights defenders face threats and intimidation.

title: Uganda Arrests 16 in Alleged $4M Fake Gold Scam
content:
Ugandan police have arrested 16 people, including four police officers, for their alleged involvement in a fake gold scam that defrauded a Dubai businessman of $4 million, the Uganda Police Force stated.

The suspects operated under the company name Real Sunnex Ltd and allegedly obtained the $4 million from an unnamed Dubai businessman through a fake gold transaction. According to investigators, the group was also preparing to obtain another $4 million from the businessman using a similar scheme. Investigators also said the four officers had abandoned their duties to guard the suspected fraudsters at an illegal gold refinery.

The investigation followed a complaint filed by the businessman in July 2025, in which he named Asiimwe Moses as one of the alleged fraudsters and identified the company as Real Sunnex Ltd. During the operation, police recovered fake gold, documents and eight vehicles.

title: Homeland Security Opens Child Exploitation Probe Into Banned Texas Volleyball Coach
content:
A Texas volleyball coach who was the subject of an investigation last month by ProPublica and The Washington Post is now facing a federal child exploitation probe, according to an agent for Homeland Security Investigations, the main investigative arm of the Department of Homeland Security.

The ProPublica and Post story detailed how Ryan Richardson continued to coach teenage girls for years at his gym in Pharr, Texas, amid allegations of misconduct, even after he was suspended in early 2025 and subsequently ruled “permanently ineligible” this February by the U.S. Center for SafeSport, an oversight group. On its public disciplinary list, SafeSport said it found that Richardson had an intimate relationship with a minor, committed sexual misconduct involving a minor, and engaged in physical misconduct and bullying.

title: Three discoveries that transformed how we understand nutrition
content:
When we think about nutrition, we almost always picture the same key players: the mouth, stomach, intestines, liver, pancreas and, perhaps, the gut microbiota. However, the human body is not made up of isolated compartments. Eating is not just about introducing food into the digestive tract, it also involves salivating, swallowing, transporting, distributing fluids, activating defences, moving fats through the lymph, connecting tissues and supporting organs.

In recent years, three body structures have attracted particular interest: the tubarial salivary glands, the interstitium and the mesentery. All three demonstrate that nutrition, hydration, absorption, transport, immunity and metabolism are closely linked.

In 2021, researchers identified previously unnoticed glandular structures at the back of the nasopharynx – near the region where the Eustachian tube opens. These glands did not fit with classical anatomical descriptions.

title: Why you should live your life like an accountant – and how you probably already do
content:
When asked to think about accounting, most people imagine numbers, calculators, spreadsheets and offices populated by smart-suited bean counters hunched over reports. You most certainly think about money.

But by breaking away from this image and reclaiming the term “accountant” to speak to a wider number of everyday activities, we can understand the vital, often positive role accounting plays in our lives.

Accounting is one of the oldest forms of communication in human history, perhaps even pre-dating other forms of written language. From these origins, it has been intrinsically linked with numerical, often financial, information.

The word account comes from the Latin verb computare, meaning to count, sum up, reckon together, which established its numerical base. Later, the French term acont tied it specifically with the counting of money – the reckoning of money received and paid. Over time, this definition has developed into our narrow association of accounting today, not only with counting, nor with the counting of money, but in particular the counting of money by a qualified professional: the accountant.

title: On Power, Truth, and Journalism
content:
In this conversation, Joseph Stiglitz, Nobel laureate and one of the world’s leading economists, reflects on the role of investigative journalism in holding power to account and informing the public.

He explores how economic and political systems shape access to information, why transparency is essential for democracy, and the challenges journalists face in making complex issues understandable and impactful.

Nobel Prize winner, Joseph Stiglitz, has been a regular speaker at GIJC. This video gathered some of his thoughts shared during the 2025 Global Investigative Journalism Conference

content:
Outokummun yli satavuotiaan kuparikaivoksen kainalossa majaansa pitävä Vanhan Kaivoksen Residenssi hakee vieraita vuodelle 2027.

Residenssi tarjoaa majoituksen ja työtilat veloituksetta taiteilijoille ja tieteilijöille, jotka haluavat tulla työskentelemään kaivoksen ainutlaatuisessa miljöössä ja kulttuuria kuplivan pikkukaupungin lämpimässä ilmapiirissä. title: Chile: Reject Constitutional Changes
content:
(Washington DC) – The Chilean Congress should reject a proposal to amend the Constitution introduced by President José Antonio Kast that would threaten a broad range of human rights, Human Rights Watch said today.

The Chilean government submitted a proposal for eight proposed constitutional amendments to the Senate on August 18, 2026, with the stated objective of enhancing the fight against organized crime. Among other things, the proposal would allow the president unfettered authority to declare states of emergency in response to anything deemed to be an imminent threat to “public security.” This would be in addition to the four types of states of emergency already provided for under the Chilean Constitution.

“The proposed constitutional amendments threaten the rights of Chileans and endanger their institutions,” said Juanita Goebertus, Americas director at Human Rights Watch. “This is a dangerous power grab that puts the rights of all Chileans at risk.”

title: Australia Probes Western Union Over Possible Money Laundering Risks
content:
Australia’s financial intelligence agency AUSTRAC has launched an investigation into Western Union Financial Services Australia and its U.S.-based parent company over concerns about how they manage money laundering and terrorism financing risks. The probe will examine the company’s anti-money laundering program, transaction monitoring and governance, including whether its systems can identify known laundering typologies and suspicious transactions linked to child sexual exploitation and terrorism financing.

The investigation follows previous regulatory engagement and an external audit ordered in 2025. Western Union operates one of the world’s largest international money transfer networks, including cash-based cross-border payments, a sector considered particularly vulnerable to criminal exploitation. Regulators have identified risks in the sector including fraud, human trafficking, terrorism financing and child sexual exploitation. title: Sanctions and bombs won’t end the war in Iran. Trump is running out of options against an intractable foe
content:
President Donald Trump has entangled the United States in a war of choice with Iran that he cannot easily win or quit.

The war was meant to be what Trump called “a little excursion” that would be over within a few weeks. But it is now into its seventh month, with no end in sight.

Trump has said he is willing to let the conflict continue for as long as needed to force Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz (which was open to free navigation before the war) and negotiate a deal over its nuclear program (even though experts say Iran was not on the verge of developing a weapon before the war).

The two sides are now in a dangerous limbo, with periodic outbreaks of fighting.

They traded strikes this week, with the US targeting Iran’s Larak island and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) retaliating with attacks on US bases in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates.

Meanwhile, there are no real negotiations toward finding a peaceful resolution to the conflict.
snippet: President Donald Trump has entangled the United States in a war of choice with Iran that he cannot easily win or quit.

title: Väitös: Lasten surun kohtaaminen sosiaalialalla edellyttää kontekstuaalis-situationaalista surutietoa
content:
Sosiaalialan ammattilaisten työssään kohtaama lasten suru kietoutuu lasten erilaisiin elämäntilanteisiin, perheen toimintatapoihin ja palvelujärjestelmän käytäntöihin. YTM Paula Vainikan väitöstutkimus osoittaa, että lasten surun tunnistaminen ja tukeminen edellyttävät ammattilaisilta kontekstuaalis-situationaalista surutietoa, joka rakentuu aina lapsen yksilöllisen tilanteen, ihmissuhteiden ja elinympäristön ymmärtämisestä.

Vainikan väitöstutkimuksessa tarkastellaan sosiaalialan ammattilaisten näkemyksiä työssään kohtaamasta lasten surusta. Tutkimuksen mukaan lasten surua ei voida ymmärtää pelkästään yksilöllisenä psykologisena kokemuksena, vaan se ilmenee ja saa merkityksensä erilaisissa sosiaalisissa, kulttuurisissa ja institutionaalisissa yhteyksissä.

Tutkimuksen keskeisenä tuloksena Vainikka muodostaa kontekstuaalis-situationaalisen surutiedon käsitteen. Se kuvaa ammattilaisten tarvitsemaa ymmärrystä siitä, miten lapsen suru rakentuu ja näyttäytyy juuri kyseisessä elämäntilanteessa, perheessä, yhteisössä ja palvelukontekstissa.

title: Terveydenhuollon digitaalinen asiointi on usein hajallaan useissa kanavissa – eAcute kokoaa asioinnin yhteen
content:
Terveydenhuollon digitaalisten palveluiden määrä on kasvanut nopeasti, mutta asiointi tapahtuu usein edelleen monissa erillisissä kanavissa. Vitec Acute vastaa tähän haasteeseen uudella eAcute-ratkaisulla, joka kokoaa potilaan digitaalisen asioinnin yhteen hallittuun kokonaisuuteen.

Digitaalinen asiointi on nykyään olennainen osa hoitopolkua, ja uusia palveluita syntyy koko ajan lisää. Ajanvaraus, viestintä, etävastaanotot sekä hoitoon liittyvät lomakkeet saattavat kuitenkin löytyä monista eri palveluista, mikä vaikeuttaa asioinnin kokonaisuuden hallintaa sekä potilaan että palveluntuottajan näkökulmasta.

eAcute kokoaa yhteen digitaalisen asioinnin kannalta keskeiset palvelut samaan palvelukokonaisuuteen. Tavoitteena on vähentää hallinnollista työtä, helpottaa tiedonkulkua ja vapauttaa ammattilaisten aikaa varsinaiseen potilastyöhön.

– Digitaalisen asioinnin pitäisi tukea hoitopolkua, ei muodostaa sen rinnalle erillisiä palvelupolkuja. Potilaan näkökulmasta asioinnin pitäisi tuntua yhdeltä kokonaisuudelta riippumatta siitä, missä vaiheessa hoitopolkua hän on, Vitec Acuten Commercial Development Manager Juuso Heponeva kertoo.

title: Rise of Chicken Shop Date highlights how YouTube turned the tables on TV
content:
Amelia Dimoldenberg says publicists ignored her interview show for years but she can now be picky over A-list guests

title: Webinar: Bringing Data Sovereignty into Participatory Sciences
content:
Wednesday 9 September at 19:00 UTC / 21:00 CEST / 3:00pm EDT (UTC -4)

The IDEAL program at the North Carolina Environmental Justice Network invites you to a webinar on Bringing Data Sovereignty into Participatory Sciences. Anna Woodroof, a researcher and program manager at IDEAL, will facilitate a conversation with Hali Dardar, a Houma scholar who created the Uke’ Contracting System for data sovereignty in the context of oral histories. We’ll also hear from Kurt Naquin, a Houma scholar, writer, and community-engaged researcher, and Caren Cooper, director of IDEAL and professor of public science. We will discuss data sovereignty and what might be possible by adapting the Uke’ system to the context of participatory science projects. We’ll explore what it could mean for individuals to retain ownership and control of their data while sharing those data with participatory projects for use and re-use. Registration is required. The guests will speak English. Live interpretation into Spanish and Portuguese will be available. Questions? Contact IDEAL@ncejn.org

title: Available: OA Switchboard plugin for OJS 3.5 | OA Switchboard
content:
Supporting Diamond journals in increasing the visibility of their open access output among research funders, institutions and consortia.

The integration plugin connecting Open Journal Systems (OJS) with the OA Switchboard is now compatible with OJS 3.5.0.x. Journals running OJS 3.5 can start using the plugin right away.

Once enabled, the plugin automatically sends a set of public article metadata to relevant research funders and institutions via the OA Switchboard when an article is published. The metadata is captured at the point of publication and shared with the institutions affiliated with the article’s authors and the funders supporting the underlying research.

This happens automatically, with no additional manual work required from the editorial team, helping diamond open access journals make their published research more visible to the organisations that fund and support it.

title: AI arkistoista innostumiseen — Maailman muisti -ohjelmalle tuotettu arkistopedagoginen oppimateriaali
content:
Tekoäly – tuo opettajien arviointityön moderni painajainen – tarjoaa oikein valjastettuna myös jatkuvasti kehittyviä mahdollisuuksia! Esimerkiksi menneisyyden vaikeaselkoiset historialliset lähteet, joita varten yliopistolla opiskeltiin vanhoja käsialoja jopa tuskan hiki otsalla helmeillen, avautuvat nyt jokaiselle muutamalla napin painalluksella! 

Miten opetamme nuoria käyttämään tekoälyä oppimisen edistäjänä ja kriittisesti tiedon tulkinnan tukena eikä oman työn korvaajana ja sokeasti luotettuna auktoriteettina? AI arkistoista innostumiseen on peruskoulun yläkouluihin ja lukioon suunnattu digitaalinen arkistopedagoginen historian oppimateriaali. Se yhdistää uudella tavalla aidot historialliset lähteet ja modernin teknologian.

title: Få tips av en ombudsman
content:
I september har många av våra specialfonder ansökningstid, varav majoriteten har inriktning på Österbotten. Vill du diskutera din ansökan med våra ombudsmän? Det kan du göra både i Karleby och via Zoom.

I september ordnar vi igen Zoom-kliniker under vilka du kan diskutera din ansökan med en ombudsman. Från och med måndagen den 7 september erbjuder Martin Enroth, vår ombudsman i Österbotten, digitala träffar där du kan få hjälp eller ställa frågor gällande din ansökan.

Martin erbjuder träffar varje måndageftermiddag i september. Träffarna är 20 minuter långa och du kan enkelt välja bland de lediga tiderna på vår bokningssida. Välj alternativet “Zoom-klinik: Ansök i september”. Här kan du boka din tid.

Vem som helst kan boka en Zoom-träff med Martin för att diskutera sin ansökan, inte bara de som ansöker från en österbottnisk specialfond.

Innan du sätter igång med din ansökan vill vi tipsa om att vi samlat alla de vanligaste frågorna vi får på vår webbplats. Fastän många tips gäller ansökningstiden i november finns där värdefull info även för dig som tänkt söka bidrag nu i september.

title: NERDS (North European Resonance and Dissonance Society)
content:
NERDS-verkoston päätavoitteena on edistää kokeellisiin musiikkiyhteisöihin liittyvää tiedon ja osaamisen vaihtoa. Lisäksi pyritään käynnistämään uusia yhteistyökuvioita sekä parantamaan yleisön mahdollisuuksia tutustua innovatiivisiin musiikkitapahtumiin ja artisteihin Pohjoismaissa ja Baltian maissa.

NERDS järjestää tapahtumia ja toimintaa, kuten festivaaleja, seminaareja ja työpajoja. Lisäksi verkosto on järjestänyt ideointitapaamisia esimerkiksi digitalisaation, taloudellisen kestävyyden, luovan tuottamisen ja markkinoinnin sekä muun tarvittavan osaamisen vahvistamiseksi. Toimet edistävät kestävää kasvua Pohjoismaiden ja Baltian maiden kokeellisen musiikin kentällä ja tukevat alan toimijoiden läsnäoloa kansainvälisellä areenalla. Verkosto järjestää kuukausittain etätapaamisia, joissa vaihdetaan tietoa kunkin festivaaliorganisaation toiminnasta ja koordinoidaan tulevia projekteja.

Pitkäkestoinen verkostotuki on osa Pohjoismaiden ja Baltian maiden kulttuurialan liikkuvuusohjelmaa, joka vahvistaa kulttuuri- ja taidealan yhteistyötä alueella.

Lue lisää verkostotuesta, muista tukiohjelmistamme ja hakuajoista täällä!

title: From Comic-Con to a Library Journal: Our Future Memory This Summer
content:
Two publications this summer put Our Future Memory in front of audiences that rarely read the same things.

The first is a report from San Diego Comic-Con. The second is a peer-reviewed article in The Political Librarian. Between them they make a case that Internet Archive Europe (IAE) has been making for years: what happens to digital collections is a public matter, and it belongs in more conversations than the ones libraries and lawyers have with each other.

On 26 July, The Beat published an account of a talk given far from the convention’s main draw.

Daniel Rasmus, a futurist who teaches scenario planning at the University of Washington, spoke at the San Diego Public Library’s Comic-Con Conference for Educators and Librarians, which brings together the librarians and teachers who use graphic novels and manga as core literacy tools. He discussed four possible futures for public libraries in an AI-saturated 2036.

title: Tim Curry (RIP) Breaks Down His Most Iconic Roles: Rocky Horror, Clue, Muppet Treasure Island & More
content:
Upon hearing of Tim Curry’s death last week, some of us could recall having seen him on stage: in Amadeus or Spamalot on Broadway, perhaps, though he also drew acclaim in the work of Stoppard, Brecht, and Shakespeare. For many more of us — perhaps all of us — it was his most memorable film and television performances that sprang to mind. To an extent, which ones are most memorable depends on the viewer. Some will forever remember Curry as DJ Johnny LaGuardia in Times Square, the deceitful Romanian philanthropist in Congo, the arch-nemesis King Chicken on Duckman, or even as the Bard himself in the series Will Shakespeare.

More will remember him as Dr. Frank-N-Furter, the cross-dressing mad scientist from the planet Transsexual at the center of the stage musical The Rocky Horror Show as well as its film adaptation The Rocky Horror Picture Show. The latter ended up becoming the much larger-scale cultural phenomenon, still screened at midnight to this day, more than half a century after its theatrical release.

title: AI Sandbox Series: A Secure Environment to Explore Artificial Intelligence at the Library
content:
This post is the first in a series about the Library of Congress Artificial Intelligence (AI) Sandbox for staff. It provides an introduction to the initiative’s goals and an overview of the types of experiments conducted so far. Future posts will feature details about experiments in text recognition and searchability, metadata and bibliographic record enhancement, and more.

As the steward of over 200 petabytes of data including manuscripts, maps, books, images, artwork, audiovisual recordings, web archives, legislative data, research reports, and copyright records, the Library of Congress has spent decades building infrastructure and services to preserve and provide access to digital materials. The predictive and generative capabilities of artificial intelligence technologies offer enticing possibilities for maintaining, delivering, and analyzing some of the nation’s most influential research and treasured cultural and historical artifacts. Yet the use of these technologies requires extensive evaluation and monitoring before implementation.

title: Ann Patchett Accepts Prize for American Fiction, Delights SRO National Book Festival Audience
content:
-NOTE: Our publication schedule was altered last week to accomodate reporting on the death of Dolly Parton. This piece, scheduled for last week, appears now. We knew you’d understand.

Ann Patchett accepted the Library’s 2026 Prize for American Fiction at the  National Book Festival, on stage with friend and fellow author Tayari Jones and in front of a standing-room-only crowd of more than 1,100 adoring fans, but she wasn’t entirely sure she wanted to be there.

“I feel like I’m too young for lifetime achievement,” she said, drawing a huge laugh from the crowd.

Patchett (62, for the record) overcame her tongue-in-cheek concerns that the honor was “the nail in the coffin” and accepted the award from Robert R. Newlen, the acting Librarian of Congress.

She might have been mollified by his description of one of the Library’s highest honors, given annually since 2008.

“The prize honors an American literary writer whose body of work is distinguished not only for its mastery of the art, but also for the originality and thought and imagination,” Newlen said.

title: Stellungnahme zum Cloud and AI Development Act
content: Mit dem CADA möchte die EU ihre technologischen Fähigkeiten im Cloud- und KI-Bereich ausbauen. Der Ansatz bietet grundsätzlich einen wirkungsvollen Rahmen, um die EU technologisch unabhängiger zu machen. Um jedoch echte Alternativen nicht bloß zur technologischen Abhängigkeit sondern auch den negativen Folgen des Hyperscaler-Modells und der Dominanz im KI-Bereich zu ermöglichen, regen wir konkrete Kriterien für eine gezielte Innovationspolitik an. Besonders wichtig sind dabei klare Regeln zur Nachhaltigkeit von Rechenzentren, die Förderung von offenen Alternativen für den Cloudmarkt und die gezielte Förderung von Cloud- und KI-Technologien mit messbarem gesellschaftlichen Mehrwert.

title: How Challengers Thrive and Competition Survives In Today’s Ecosystem
content:
The web should be a place where people can choose how they connect, which tools they use, and who they trust. At Mozilla, we live these values, prioritizing products that ensure users can control their experience and that the web remains a global public resource.

Challengers across the tech ecosystem provide these competitive opportunities, but they contend with structural barriers imposed by tech giants leveraging market dominance. A healthy internet depends on ensuring that independent companies have a fair opportunity to innovate and compete on merit. That’s why Mozilla and many others support key legislation like AICOA.

So how do we promote proposals like AICOA and ensure that challengers can thrive in markets controlled by powerful gatekeepers?  We explored these questions and more at the recent Mozilla Meetup, “How Challengers Thrive: Why Competition Matters for AI, Security, and the Open Internet.”  Across panel events, a lightning discussion, and a networking happy hour, we discussed promoting an innovative, secure internet.

title: Von der Leyen set to deliver major speech on Europe’s space policy
content:
BRUSSELS — European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will deliver a major speech dedicated solely to space at the International Space Summit in Paris on Sept. 10, two officials working on preparations for the event told POLITICO.

The address comes as the Commission prepares to unveil its European Space Shield, an action plan aimed at protecting the bloc’s satellites and other space assets in what officials increasingly describe as an increasingly hostile security environment.

French President Emmanuel Macron is convening a two-day International Space Summit at Paris’ Grand Palais venue on Sept. 9-10. It is expected to bring together delegations from more than 120 countries alongside space agencies, industry leaders, scientists and military officials.

Von der Leyen’s participation in the event has not been previously reported.

title: Belarus: Authorities targeting European Humanities University students abroad and their families in intensifying crackdown
content:
Reacting to a growing number of reports that Belarusian authorities are persecuting, intimidating and targeting students and others connected to the European Humanities University (EHU) in Vilnius, Lithuania, as part of their efforts to repress dissent beyond Belarus’ borders, Marie Struthers, Amnesty International’s Director for Eastern Europe and Central Asia, said:

“As the new academic year begins, the Belarusian authorities’ relentless campaign against the exiled European Humanities University has taken a disturbing new turn, intensifying its assault on the rights to education, freedom of expression and academic freedom. This campaign of intimidation is no longer confined to students and others connected to the independent Belarusian university in Lithuania. They now extend to relatives and associates in Belarus, illustrating how the authorities’ brazen repressive tactics reach far beyond the country’s borders.”

“Mounting reports show that dozens of people in Belarus are subjected to searches, interrogations, detention and threats, and forced to pressure their loved ones to quit the university and return to Belarus.

title: Why solidarity is vital to freeing imprisoned human rights defenders
content:
By Mandeep Tiwana, Secretary General and Susan Marx, Chief Programmes Officer

Every Aug. 30, the world marks the International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disappearances. Beneath the official statements and solemn commemorations lies a stark, unsettling reality: the practice of making people vanish — and holding them in silence away from the world — remains a favored tactic for powerful regimes seeking to crush dissent. The goal of authoritarian states is to cut dissenters off from the outside world until public attention fades. 

Yet as New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani highlighted during a global leadership summit last month, solidarity is far more than a moral sentiment; when organized effectively, it acts as a concrete strategy to pull those trapped in state-enforced shadows back into the light.

title: Bringing the Climate Frontlines to the Red Carpet
content:
Greetings from the Venice International Film Festival, where amidst the cinematic glamour, we are launching something raw and powerful: “Solwata”.

It is an immense privilege to be here sharing this new immersive documentary—co-created with the communities of Walande, Ngongosila, and Kwai in Solomon Islands, co-produced with Human Rights Watch, Agog, and NowHere Media, and narrated by Mark Ruffalo—bringing the realities of climate relocation to this global stage.

A mixed reality experience narrated by Academy Award–nominated actor and climate and human rights advocate Mark Ruffalo, Solwata puts viewers inside the slow-motion climate catastrophe as communities contemplate uncertain futures and reconstruct home.

When first approached by colleagues about using extended reality for advocacy, I had doubts. As a researcher, I typically rely on exhaustively fact-checked reports with detailed footnotes to convey findings. But seeing how deeply moved the audience is as they step out of headsets, I am won over.

title: EEPA reports on ENDF base in Asosa expands military activity
content:
BRUSSELS | 31 August 2026 (IDN | EEPA) — The following are the situation reports on Sudan, Ethiopia, Night-time curfew lifted in Khartoum, ENDF base in Asosa expands military activity, 2 peacekeepers killed in South Sudan.

  • The night-time curfew and state of emergency in Khartoum has been lifted after two years, allowing people to travel and work without overnight restrictions, while all other security measures remain in place, including patrols, checkpoints and identity checks.
  • 2.1 million Sudanese returnees arrived in Khartoum state after being forcibly displaced due to war, says a report by the UNHCR.
  • The recovery of the capital city, however, remains fragile and incomplete with residents facing unreliable electricity and water, unemployment, inflation, costly transport and worsening environmental problems, and severely disrupted education and health care systems.
  • Many returnees also struggle to find safe, affordable housing, while being exposed to unexploded weapons, looting and night-time insecurity, leaving families vulnerable to renewed displacement.

title: Mikael Wigell: Yrityksen oma data näytti 15 prosentin Kiina-altistumaa – todellinen osuus oli lähes 90 prosenttia
content:
Yritysten käsitys toimitusketjujensa geopoliittisista riskeistä voi jäädä pahasti todellisuudesta. Economic Security Forumin selvittämässä tapauksessa eurooppalaisen teknologiayrityksen oma toimittajadata osoitti 15 prosentin Kiina-altistumaa, mutta toimitusketjun syväkartoituksessa osuus nousi lähes 90 prosenttiin.

Economic Security Forumin perustaja ja toimitusjohtaja Mikael Wigell esitteli tapauksen Profession Procurement Executive 2026 -tapahtumassa Helsingissä. Hänen mukaansa perinteinen toimittaja-auditointi ei enää riitä, koska suurimmat geopoliittiset riippuvuudet löytyvät usein suorien toimittajien takaa.

– Yrityksen oma toimittajadata näytti 15 prosentin altistumaa Kiinalle. Kun toimitusketjua kartoitettiin yli 4 000 tehtaaseen asti, altistumaksi paljastui lähes 90 prosenttia, Wigell sanoi.

Yritykset tuntevat yleensä ensimmäisen tason toimittajansa, mutta näkyvyys heikkenee nopeasti toimitusketjun seuraavilla tasoilla. Nimellisesti toisistaan riippumattomat toimittajat saattavat käyttää samoja tehtaita, materiaaleja tai logistisia reittejä.

title: Epävarmuuden ja toivottomuuden ajasta täytyy löytää ulospääsy

title: Countries legally obliged to consider slavery reparations, says UN committee
content:
Guidance says states must implement ‘comprehensive measures’ to address legacy of racial discrimination

A UN committee has said countries are legally obliged to consider reparations for the transatlantic slave trade and take other ⁠measures to address the enduring ⁠legacy of racial ​discrimination.

Guidance published on Monday by the committee on the elimination of racial discrimination (CERD) said the obligations arose from ⁠a legally binding 1965 convention on racial discrimination, not from the legal standards that existed when the slave trade took place.

title: Do Ukrainian women subject to military service have to leave the EU?
content:
At the end of July, the European Union (EU) did indeed extend temporary protection for people displaced from Ukraine until the 4th of March 2028. At the same time, new applicants for temporary protection will have to be able to demonstrate that they have complied with the military obligations laid down in Ukrainian law.

“Given Ukraine’s evolving defence needs, temporary protection going forward will only be granted to those who have fulfilled their military service obligations in Ukraine,” the Council of the European Union states in its announcement. This can be demonstrated, for example, by a passport containing an exit stamp issued by the Ukrainian authorities showing that the person left Ukraine legally. A paper or electronic document confirming an exemption from military obligations or their fulfilment can also be used as evidence.

title: How Cyber Sleuths Tracked a Nigerian Scammer to His Doorstep
content:
This is an adaption of a podcast interview 404 Media recorded with Erin West and Paul Raffile. Check out the whole thing here on YouTube.

Erin West and Paul Raffile stepped out of their van about 45 minutes outside Lagos, Nigeria, and walked down a muddy hill. At the bottom, they entered a field with houses made of corrugated steel and cardboard. Raffile kept falling into the mud.

After walking about a quarter of a mile, the pair came to a hut, six feet high on stilts, and climbed up a ladder. Inside was the baba lao, a local spiritual leader. The baba lao was going to do a ritual designed to ensure a Nigerian scammer would make more money in his blackmailing or manipulation of an overseas victim, maybe back in the United States.

A scammer who accompanied West and Raffile had a photo of the victim he was trying to get money from, and the identity he had impersonated to do so. The baba lao then fused these two souls together to bring more fortune to the scammer, Raffile recalled. For two and a half hours, the baba lao jumped between grinding herbs, creating talismans, sacrificing an animal. Locals gathered outside the hut.

title: Investigating a Murder: Public Records Uncover New Clues in Chinatown Cold Case
content:
Sign up here to receive Bellingcat’s biggest investigations by email as soon as they are published.

On a June night in 1996, in a basement apartment in Boston’s Chinatown, a killer put a pistol to the back of a young man’s head and pulled the trigger. The victim’s body was wrapped in quilts, lowered into the trunk of a car and driven about 20 miles southwest of the city, where it was dumped in the woods. It lay undiscovered through two New England winters until a dog walked home carrying a human bone. 

For three decades, authorities did not release the victim’s name to the public. He is listed in the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System (NamUs) as #UP12385, one of 202 unidentified people recorded in the state of Massachusetts. The circumstances of his discovery are reduced to five words: “Skeletal remains found in woods.” The case remains unsolved.

title: South Africa Arrests Suspect in $37M Hospital Corruption Case
content:
South Africa’s Hawks arrested a 37-year-old man in an investigation into corruption, procurement fraud and money laundering involving 635 million rand ($37 million) at Tembisa Hospital. He was detained at Johannesburg’s O.R. Tambo International Airport after returning from abroad. Investigators say hospital officials colluded with service providers to keep individual transactions below 500,000 rand and bypass formal tender procedures. He is expected to face fraud, corruption and money laundering charges in a Specialized Commercial Crimes Court. Authorities have not named the man.

The arrest is part of a broader investigation into claims that more than 2 billion rand was looted from the public hospital. South Africa’s Special Investigating Unit previously identified three coordinated syndicates that it says used networks of companies and thousands of irregular transactions to divert hospital funds. The procurement activity was initially flagged by Gauteng Health Department whistleblower Babita Deokaran, who was murdered in 2021.

title: California Lawmakers Pass Bill to Punish Administrators Who Fail to Vet Teachers for Misconduct
content:
California lawmakers unanimously passed legislation last week to ensure that school administrators are informed about past accusations of misconduct against teachers as part of their hiring process.  

The legislation follows a KQED-ProPublica investigation revealing how delays and inaction, combined with a lack of transparency, allowed educators to get new jobs after school districts reported them to the state teacher licensing agency for sexual harassment or other misconduct. Our reporting found that at least 14 educators were hired by new schools after their former employers determined they had sexually harassed students or committed other sexual misconduct.

title: Luovien alojen yhteiset kannat työttömyysturvan kehittämiseen
content:
Nykyinen ansiosidonnainen turva perustuu selkeään jakoon työttömien, työntekijöiden ja yrittäjien välillä. Tällöin taide- ja kulttuurialan ammattilaiset jäävät herkästi turvaverkon väliinputoajiksi, sillä alalle on tyypillistä, että tulot kertyvät useasta eri lähteestä. Osa näistä tulolähteistä ei ole tällä hetkellä minkään vakuutuksen piirissä. Esimerkiksi apurahalla työskentely ei kartuta ansiosidonnaisten etuuksien työssäoloehtoa, vaikka monille taide- ja kulttuurialan ammattilaisille apurahat ovat keskeinen osa toimeentuloa.

Yhtenä ratkaisuna on esitetty yhdistelmävakuutusta. Yhdistelmävakuutus kohentaisi erityisesti niiden ihmisten asemaa, jotka

  • saavat tuloja sekä palkan- ja apurahansaajana että yrittäjänä
  • eivät tällä hetkellä täytä palkansaajan tai yrittäjän työssäoloehtoa erikseen arvioituna
  • täyttäisivät työssäoloehdon, jos kaiken työssäolon voisi laskea yhteen.

title: The EU’s repair policies are changing the way tech is designed
content:
In the late 1970s, concerned by resource use and scarcity, German industrial designer Dieter Rams developed his “ten principles for good design”. Among other things, he argued for design that is long-lasting and environmentally friendly. Half a century later, his concerns are more relevant than ever.

According to the UN’s Global E-waste Monitor, the amount of e-waste generated worldwide almost doubled from 2010 to 2022, and is projected to increase by another 32% by 2030. One driver is the growing number of new devices. According to Eurostat, the amount of electrical and electronic equipment put on the EU market rose from 7.6 million tonnes in 2012 to 14.4 million in 2023.

Currently, less than a third of this gets recycled, but recycling is just one way of putting the brakes on this trend. Keeping products in use by prolonging their lifespan can deliver even greater environmental benefits.

Repair is vitally important to making this happen, but current options are often limited or unaffordable. When a device breaks, consumers can struggle to find repair information, let alone spare parts. This means it is often easier, quicker and cheaper to buy a whole new device.

title: ”Naisten oma pankki” auttaa, kun muualta ei saa luottoa – Hellen Matheri on yksi monista säästöryhmiin kuuluneista naisista
content:
Miten sinä rahoittaisit elämäsi, jos pankista ei saisi lainaa? 

Kuulin ensimmäisen kerran äitien omista rahoista keskustellessani suomensomalialaisen ystäväni kanssa. Perheeseen oli tehty suurempi ostos, kenties huonekalu, tai ehkä joku lapsista oli lähetetty opiskelemaan. Transaktion välineenä oli käytetty äidin ystäväpiirin omaa lainajärjestelmää, somalialaisen diasporan tuliaista, ayuutoa. 

Rahajärjestelmän nimellä on eurooppalaiset juuret: aiuto tarkoittaa apua italiaksi. Se voi olla siirtomaahistorian seurausta, sillä Italia miehitti Somalian niemimaan vuonna 1889.  

Myös hagbadina tunnetulla järjestelmällä on pitkät perinteet Somaliassa. Kyseessä on  epävirallinen säästö- ja lainaryhmittymä, jonka piiriin kuuluvat henkilöt lainaavat toisilleen rahaa yhdessä laadittujen sääntöjen puitteissa, ilman korkeaa korkoa. 
 
Järjestelmät tunnetaan table banking -yleisnimellä, mutta kansainvälisesti niille löytyy yli 200 paikallista nimitystä. Intian, Pakistanin ja Bangladeshin alueella käytetään nimitystä chit funds, Perussa nimeä panderos tai juntas, kun taas kiinankielisessä maailmassa tunnetaan hui– tai hehui-verkostot.

title: The music that made Dolly Parton a global icon
content:
It was 1967, and country musician Porter Wagoner was introducing a guest on his weekly TV show.

The camera cuts to a woman with big, blonde beehive, wearing a magenta mini dress with the same shade of lipstick to match. It was in that moment a star was born.

Her name was Dolly Parton. In the following decades after that performance, Parton went on to become the “Queen of Country”.

But as musicologist and professor of music at Hamilton College in the US, Lydia Hamessley told The Conversation Weekly podcast, Parton’s music drew inspiration from across the board.

I heard so many resonances in her music of old-timey Appalachian or mountain music.

Her expressive way of singing felt like she had grown up hearing people singing in a particular way, that had such a heart to it and such a power to her voice.

title: Explainer: The CMIP7 emissions scenarios – and how they explore future climate change
content:
Every six to seven years, climate modelling groups around the world run a coordinated set of simulations that explore how the climate could change in the future. 

These simulations form a key line of evidence for future projections used in Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) assessment reports. 

They are built around a set of common scenarios – or “pathways” – of future greenhouse gas emissions.

A new set of scenarios has now been published for the seventh phase of the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP7). 

These replace the scenarios that drove the previous generation of climate models and featured heavily in the IPCC’s sixth assessment report (AR6).

The new scenarios are different from their predecessors – known as the “shared socioeconomic pathways” (SSPs) – in a number of notable ways.

Rather than being named, somewhat enigmatically, according to their “radiative forcing levels”, the new scenarios are named simply by their emissions trajectories – ranging from “low-to-negative” to “high”. 

They no longer consider “no-climate-policy” baseline worlds, but instead explore the implications of current policies continuing, being strengthened, or weakening.

title: Negotiating AI Limits and Biological Weapons
content:
Earlier this month, US researchers used AI to design new viruses for the first time. Though these viruses were created only to combat bacteria like E. coli, the breakthrough has led to increased calls for international agreements to regulate the use of AI to develop biological weapons.

However, one drawback of our current unipolar moment is that the US has become unaccustomed to negotiating formal agreements with its opponents. In any case, there is currently a lack of interest in formal agreements. 

What would it take to actually get agreement on AI?

First, there must be a shared perception of risk and threat. The Cuban Missile Crisis inspired a generation of agreements for nuclear weapons, conventional military action, and WMD. Leaders in both Russia and the United States remembered their experiences in World War II and feared the return of global war fueled by nuclear weapons. This common understanding created the basis for negotiation and, ultimately, agreement.

title: ‘Moving Just One Block in Port-Au-Prince Was Equivalent to Traveling Nearly 1,000km Elsewhere in the World’: The Challenges of Ethnographic Journalism in Haiti
content:
For over a decade, the Salvadoran journalist and anthropologist Juan José Martínez D’Aubuisson has used the practice of ethnographic journalism to explore violence and how gang-related crime has impacted communities across the Americas.

His reporting from Honduras, the Dominican Republic, and Haiti, to mention some of his most recent work, has won awards: In 2024, he received the Ortega y Gasset Award from El País for The Moskitia: The Honduran Jungle Drowning in Cocaine, a piece documenting the destruction of Central America’s largest rainforest by drug trafficking. That same year, Massacre Border, his investigation into the violence faced by Haitians in the Dominican Republic, was shortlisted for an award from the True Story Festival. In 2025, his investigation Searching for Mikelson: An Apartheid in the Caribbean won the prestigious Gabo Award in the text category.

title: Read Now – Disaster Risk Reduction and Open Data Newsletter: August 2026 Edition
content:
A data engineering approach to tracking global climate resilience

What counts as a climate-resilient road? One country might build to withstand a 1-in-50-year flood, another a 1-in-100-year flood, and both report against the same indicator. COP30 in Belém adopted 59 indicators for the Global Goal on Adaptation. Bapon Fakhruddin of the Green Climate Fund and Matti Heikkurinen of CODATA warn that figures which look comparable often are not. Their answer is not a single global standard but the Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework, which acts as a translator between existing sectoral standards, so communities need not change how they collect data. Building it in from the outset costs far less than retrofitting it and decides whether the Global Stocktake measures genuine progress or merely records the attempt to describe it.

title: The Periodic Table of Endangered Elements: Visualizing the Chemical Elements That Could Vanish Before You Know It
content:
The Periodic Table of Elements lists the 118 chemical elements that make up everything in our world. Some you’re familiar with—Hydrogen, Oxygen, Nitrogen, etc. Others maybe less so—Vanadium, Germanium, and Yttrium.

According to the American Chemical Society, 44 of those 118 elements might disappear by century’s end. Enter the Periodic Table of Endangered Elements (shown above). The most endangered ones, highlighted in red, are Zinc, Gallium, Germanium, Arsenic (is this a good or very bad thing?), Silver, Indium, Tellurium, and Hafnium. Made available under a Creative Commons license, the Periodic Table of Endangered Elements can be viewed in a larger format here.

The original image (top of the page), created in 2015, was updated by EuChemS in 2023 (above). The updated table features the current-day availability of all 90 elements, rather than just the endangered 44 elements, adds an axis for sustainability, and flags elements used in smartphone production.

title: EFF to Courts: Don’t Rewrite Copyright Over AI Hype
content:
The history of technology is rife with copyright panics.  In the 1980s, major rightsholders ran to Congress and the courts, claiming that videotape recorders (VTR) were “to the American film producer and the American public as the Boston strangler is to the woman home alone.” Then, the Supreme Court declined to embrace the hype, noting that the VTR was capable of all kinds of non-infringing uses, like time-shifting and cautioning courts to avoid rewriting copyright law in response to new technologies. We believe that courts now should be similarly wary about the hype surrounding AI.

Hollywood’s hyperbole has echoed that of composer John Phillip Sousa, who claimed in 1906 that the player piano and the gramophone would destroy music composition; portrait artists who feared the camera would replace the paintbrush. None of these things happened. Cameras, for example, sparked a resurgence of portraiture and, by making it possible for more people to create images, led to unexpected developments—like the rise of photojournalism.

title: Power-hungry data centers are expanding in Europe. So is the resistance.
content:
KRONSTORF, Austria — One sleepy village nestled in the foothills of the Alps may soon devour more electricity than all the households of Vienna.

It is all thanks to Google.

The American tech giant is building Austria’s first hyperscale data center on the outskirts of tiny Kronstorf, a two-hour drive from the capital. The site could eventually consume the equivalent of 7 percent of the country’s current power demand.

Growing resistance, however, may throw a wrench in the company’s ambitions. A band of local rebels — worried about the data center’s voracious appetite for energy and skeptical about a power grab by a U.S. tech behemoth — is battling to prevent expansion.

“We really want to give them a hard time,” said Harald Müllner, an IT specialist from nearby Linz, who co-founded a local alliance of scientists, artists and activists campaigning against the data center. “They need to see that the people are not happy with this.”

title: Tibet Flood Victims Have a Right to be Heard
content:
As people in Nepal and across the Chinese border in Tibet reel from horrific mudslides, the Chinese government has turned to censorship and control.

On Weibo, which follows Beijing’s censorship demands, the Chinese social media platform prominently pinned a memorial hashtag (#向吉隆泥石流灾害遇难人员默哀) at the top of trending topics, alongside eight other disaster-related topics. The lead post featured a CCTV newscaster essentially reading a Politburo communique, during which President Xi Jinping reportedly suggested China's top leaders observe a minute of silence for the victims.

Censorship and self-censorship are pervasive throughout China, particularly in Tibetan areas, as Human Rights Watch has long documented. People can be imprisoned for undermining national security simply by sharing information with the outside world. Foreigners, including journalists and independent investigators, are unable to enter without permission.

title: ‘Breakthrough’ as Turkmenistan starts fixing ‘mindboggling’ methane mega-leaks
content:
Secretive state begins repairs on ageing facilities after being revealed as worst country for leaks of potent greenhouse gas

Turkmenistan has started plugging the mega-leaks of methane that spew from its ageing oil and gas facilities, the latest UN data shows, in a move hailed as a breakthrough.

Methane, also called natural or fossil gas, is a potent greenhouse gas. It traps 80 times more heat than carbon dioxide and causes 25% of global heating today. Stopping leaks can be quick and cheap and, because methane breaks down in the atmosphere far quicker than CO2, this has a rapid impact, with some experts calling it the climate “emergency brake”.

title: Is the European Comission planning to confiscate 90% of people’s wealth?
content:
Although Latvia is not among the countries mentioned in the video, one user on the social media platform X has already claimed that “the EC is looking into dekulakisation measures. So that everyone can be equal. Admirable. Let’s tighten our belts and chip in. Some 9 million [euros], not expensive”.

Kužnieks told Delfi that the claims made in the video had been checked by the Representation. The EC is not planning to freeze people’s bank accounts or confiscate 50% or 90% of their wealth, as claimed in the video. The Commission has also not identified any countries where such measures could be introduced first. Nor is the Commission proposing any measures to tax wealth.

The video circulating on social media uses a real study commissioned by the Commission, but its content is interpreted misleadingly. In 2026, the Directorate-General for Taxation and Customs Union (DG TAXUD) published a study aimed at gaining a better understanding of different wealth-related taxes, their interaction with one another and their effects. title: The Trump Administration’s Plan for Protecting Consumers? Politely Ask Companies to Behave.
content:
In mid-July testimony before Congress, Russell Vought boasted that, as the acting head of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, he’d refashioned the agency’s approach to pursuing banks and other financial companies accused of exploiting Americans — the role Congress had created for the agency after the 2008 economic crash.

Vought had spent the first 18 months of the new Trump administration trying to dismantle the bureau, much as he and other appointees had done with the U.S. Agency for International Development. At CFPB, he’d ordered mass layoffs, tried to choke off the bureau’s funding and ended the lease on its headquarters, attempting to make good on his vow to put civil servants “in trauma.” But federal courts blocked Vought’s efforts to close the CFPB, with a judge at one point saying the administration had acted with “complete disregard” for Congress.

title: Southeast Asia Shows Surprising Semiconductor Strengths
content:
It’s the indispensable back end of the Western semiconductor stack. Malaysia, the Philippines, and Singapore form a critical trio for the assembly, testing, and advanced packaging of semiconductors.

The Southeast Asian trio does not aim to replicate Taiwanese-style leading‑edge fabs. They are doubling down on their existing back‑end strengths and upgrading their skills to service automotive, defense, and AI chips. For all three countries, semiconductors represent a key industry, and each specializes in a specific part of the value chain. 

The Philippines, the least-developed economy of the three, leverages its English-speaking technical workforce. Multinational chipmakers including Intel, Texas Instruments, and Analog Devices run large Filipino operations. They import raw wafers to assemble, package, and test. 

The economic impact is immense. Electronics account for almost 60% of the Philippines’ goods exports, with about three-quarters, or about $31 billion per year, attributable to semiconductors.

title: Doxxing Safety Part II: Incident Response
content:
Doxxing, also known as the deliberate sharing of personal information to harass or endanger someone, is a tricky thing to protect against. It often happens by some ill-intentioned person accessing publicly available information, then sharing that information more widely in the hopes it will intimidate their target or worse. 

This guide is a followup from a previous post that describes a methodology for you to clean up your digital footprint and get a firm entry into the art of open source intelligence. There's a slight bit of repetition here, but with a slant towards using those now-familiar tools and methods toward what to do in the context of incident response. The best thing you can do is familiarize yourself with this post and its tactics before something happens, then return back to it for reference when needed.

title: Trump: Communities that reject data centers will end up ‘backwards and poor’
content:
President Donald Trump on Monday again championed the spread of data centers despite growing bipartisan backlash ahead of the midterms in November.

In a post to Truth Social, the president insisted data centers will lead to richer, more successful Americans and criticized those who object to them.

“The only reason that communities throughout the U.S.A. should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor,” Trump said. “If we kill the Golden Goose, you will only have yourselves to blame.”

Data center expansion has become a critical component in the leadup to November’s midterms, with polls showing a majority of Americans oppose them being built in their communities. Republicans and Democrats alike have expressed concerns over data centers, with lawmakers and state leaders warning about overloaded power grids, strained water systems and the level of noise the projects create.
snippet: President Donald Trump on Monday again championed the spread of data centers despite growing bipartisan backlash ahead of the midterms in November.

title: How Croatian communities are taking on planned poultry slaughterhouses
content:
Over 51,000 people signed a petition challenging the state’s lack of transparency and allegations of favoritism

Originally published on Global Voices

A chicken. Photo by David Goehring via Flickr, CC BY 2.0.

Sisak, a city known for its manufacturing industry and for operating the second largest oil refinery in Croatia, has been receiving an unusual amount of media coverage about chickens. Citizens have come out in their numbers against a series of proposed industrial poultry facilities, which locals and non-governmental organizations (NGOs) claim will have an adverse effect on the natural environment, reduce living standards, and engage in the inhumane treatment of animals.

By April 2026, protest organizers said they had identified 24 planned poultry projects across three Croatian counties, being advanced separately by two investors: agricultural conglomerate MHP (formerly Myronivsky Hliboprodukt), one of the largest poultry companies in Europe, and Premium Chicken Company (PCC), owned by the Croatian holding company Renaissance Capital d.o.o. (LLC), not to be confused with the similarly named Moscow-based investment bank Renaissance Capital (RenCap).

title: Nigeria: Foreign Aid Bill Endangers Civil Society
content:
(Abuja) – A proposed law to regulate foreign aid risks undermining the independence of civil society organizations and shrinking civic space in Nigeria, Human Rights Watch said today. The National Assembly should reject provisions that would give authorities undue influence over the funding and activities of independent organizations. 

In May 2026, the Senate introduced the Foreign Aid (Regulation, Transparency and Disclosure) Bill, which seeks to regulate the use of foreign aid, grants, and donations in Nigeria. The bill would establish a regulatory commission to oversee foreign aid. The bill says its intention is to promote transparency and accountability, align aid with national development priorities, prevent the misuse and duplication of projects, and improve public access to information about foreign-funded activities.

title: Latvia’s request for a 7 billion euro EU grant remains only an idea for now
content:
Following the publication of the article, many questions arose about whether Latvia had already requested this funding from the EU, when a decision by the EU institutions might be expected and how the money could be spent. However, as Delfi has established, Latvia has not yet discussed the allocation of such funds with EU institutions or other member states – it remains only an idea. Moreover, no meetings specifically devoted to the issue have been planned so far.

According to Politico, Kulbergs’ argument for why the EU should allocate the 7 billion euros to Latvia is that Latvia has to borrow money to ensure the security of countries that are much further from the frontline. The article states that these funds, which Latvia wants in addition to funding already earmarked for other countries, would account for almost half of the planned 15.12 billion euros in defence spending during the new EU multiannual budget period.

However, in comments to Delfi, the prime minister explained that the 7 billion euros is intended in the form of a grant, while stressing that “this is currently only at the level of an idea and discussions between all the eastern-flank countries and the EU are needed”.

title: He Spent 27 Years on Death Row as a Wrongfully Convicted Man. What Comes Next?
content:
Jimmie “Chris” Duncan wiped the sweat off his forehead as he assessed his temporary home from the parking lot of a rundown motel in central Louisiana. Sure, there’s drug dealing and prostitution, he said on a recent summer afternoon. And he suspected his neighbors were cooking meth on a floor below the room he paid $350 a week to rent.

But, he said, “I feel safe here. I mean, I’ve been on death row. I feel safe anywhere.”

Duncan had spent the last three decades trying to prove his innocence after a jury convicted him of killing his former girlfriend’s toddler. An investigation by Verite News and ProPublica last year showed that prosecutors had relied on key evidence that appeared to be fabricated by a pair of forensics experts whose use of bite mark analysis has since been widely discredited as junk science.

title: Voiko Himalajan katastrofi olla ilmastotaistelun käännekohta?
content:
Johanna Kohvakka

Himalajalla tapahtui viime viikon keskiviikkona katastrofi, jonka lopullista mittakaavaa ei vieläkään tiedetä.

Nepalin ja Tiibetin rajaseudulla Langtang Lirungin alueella irtosi valtava määrä jäätä ja kiveä. Romahdus käynnisti vyöryn, joka muuttui laaksoissa valtavaksi veden, mudan, jään ja kiviaineksen virraksi. Rakennuksia, teitä ja siltoja katosi sen mukana.

Maanantaihin mennessä Nepalissa oli vahvistettu kuolleeksi 1 007 ja kateissa oli yli 4 600. Kiinan puolella Tiibetissä kuolleita oli 16 ja kateissa 546. Yhteensä kuolleita on siis jo yli tuhat ja kateissa yli 5 100. Kadonneiden joukossa on satoja ulkomaalaisia. Luvut voivat edelleen muuttua pelastustöiden jatkuessa. Todennäköisesti Kiinan puolelta ilmoitetut luvut ovat puutteellisia.

Katastrofin välitön tapahtumaketju alkaa olla selvillä. Satelliittikuvat ja seismiset havainnot osoittavat, että jäätikön yhteydessä tapahtui valtava kallio- ja jäämassan romahdus. Aluksi maanjäristykseksi tulkittu seisminen signaali syntyikin romahduksesta itsestään.

title: Doxxing Safety Pt I: Prevention and Footprint Management
content:
Doxxing is the deliberate disclosure of personal information in order to bully, harass, intimidate, or instigate a chain of harms against someone. It's a tricky thing to protect against when the jerk doing it is often able to use legal and accessible means to do so. The odds are stacked against everyday internet folk when there's little to no comprehensive data privacy legislation keeping us safe. The responsibility is on each of us to protect ourselves, but the good news is that there's a lot you can do to reduce your digital footprint and take control of your data.

This post is part one of a two-part series discussing safety and response to doxxing. This first part focuses on prevention and ways to reduce your overall footprint. The second focuses on incident response, as in, steps to take if you're in the midst of being doxxed. There will be some crossover and redundancy between these two posts, so it's worth reading each and gaining familiarity with the steps well ahead of time.

title: EU places ChatGPT, Reddit, Roblox under its strictest platform rules
content:
The European Commission has placed ChatGPT, Reddit and Roblox under its toughest regulatory regime for online services.

On Monday, the Commission designated ChatGPT as a Very Large Online Search Engine and Reddit and Roblox as Very Large Online Platforms under its Digital Services Act. These labels place U.S.-based services under the Commission’s direct supervision, imposing obligations to assess and mitigate systemic risks, including effects on minors, election integrity, and public security.

Should a company fail to comply with the rules within four months, it risks fines of up to six percent of its annual global revenue.

Online services with more than 45 million users in the EU are subject to the stricter regime, which now includes 28 platforms and search engines.

ChatGPT’s potential designation has been closely watched since it declared 120 million users last year. But the Commission has had a hard time deciding whether the flagship service run by OpenAI is a search engine or a platform. The popular chatbot credited with ushering in the current artificial intelligence revolution is already closely regulated in Brussels through the Artificial Intelligence Act.
snippet: The European Commission has placed ChatGPT, Reddit and Roblox under its toughest regulatory regime for online services.
creator: Eliza Gkritsi
sourceDescription: European Politics, Policy, Government News

content:
Andris Sprūds is now the Progressives’ lead candidate in the Vidzeme constituency in the upcoming parliamentary elections. Delfi contacted Sprūds and the Ministry of Defence (MoD) to fact-check the claim.

Andris Kulbergs made the claim while answering questions about drone incidents and the work of former Defence Minister Sprūds. Asked whether he was referring to systems purchased during Sprūds’ tenure for which the necessary munitions had not been bought, the prime minister declined to give a specific answer. “We bought the equipment, but forgot to buy the munitions,” Kulbergs said on the programme, adding that such a situation had occurred. He did not name the specific procurement, system, or institution responsible for failing to purchase the ammunition.

The MoD told Delfi that the munitions had not been forgotten. However, a dispute had arisen between the minister and the National Armed Forces (NAF) over their procurement, which had taken up valuable time.

title: Privacy on the Map (Part 2): Progress, Pitfalls, and the Fight for Enforceable Location Data Protections
content:
Regulating commercial location tracking has reached a turning point. Last year, we published our rubric for what comprehensive and protective location privacy laws should look like, outlining the baseline standards states should meet to shield individuals from pervasive location surveillance. Since then, state lawmakers across the country have begun responding to calls like these, with Connecticut, Maryland, New Jersey, Oregon, and Virginia enacting new consumer privacy restraints on an industry that profits off our physical movements.

Yet, even as these states move the ball forward to restrict location tracking, most of their laws leave significant gaps that still must be filled. Other states – and Congress – need to get into the game, too, and ensure protection of everyone.

Imagine spending a couple of hours in a coffee shop, a friend's house, or a healthcare clinic, only to discover yourself under police investigation because your cell phone’s location data exposed your presence there.

title: China’s latest curbs on EU firms look symbolic. That could change.
content:
VILNIUS — China’s latest trade restrictions on EU companies are unlikely to hurt much — for now. But its choice of targets shows how Beijing could make future retaliation far more painful.

China hit 14 EU entities last month with export curbs on so-called dual-use items that have both civilian and military uses. Beijing’s move amounted to a tit-for-tat retaliation after the EU listed the same number of Chinese companies in July in a round of Russia-related sanctions for allegedly aiding Vladimir Putin’s four-year-old war against Ukraine. 

While five European companies that were listed told POLITICO they would be able to cope with the measures, Beijing’s choice of targets has experts and business leaders worried that any future restrictions would expose Europe’s dependence on China for the supply of critical industry inputs.

“It’s sending a signal. Just think twice: Would you be able to further conduct that business without supplies from China?” Aldas Juronis, CEO of specialized laser company Ekspla, said in an interview.

Ekspla is among the 14 EU firms now barred from receiving Chinese dual-use items.

title: “Romania is annexing Moldova”: how frightening disinformation exploded within a few hours
content:
It all began on the 24th of June, when Romania’s lower house of parliament, the Chamber of Deputies, technically deemed a bill submitted by the far-right and pro-Russian party S.O.S. România on the unification of Romania and Moldova to have been “adopted by tacit approval”. The bill stipulates that, once it enters into force, the Romanian government would be authorised to “urgently and immediately” begin negotiations with Chisinau on “completing the union with the Republic of Moldova”, Romanian news portal Digi24 explains.

Before explaining what “tacit approval” means and why such a proposal from a radical party does not have broad political support that would allow it to become law, let us turn to what happened next in the information space.

It took only a few hours for the claim that Romania had effectively begun annexing Moldova to spread like wildfire with the help of various actors and anonymous social media accounts.

content: Abstract: The rise of Diamond Open Access (DOA) represents a major transformation in scholarly communication, redefining traditional systems of knowledge distribution. Diamond open access model has gained recognition as the most equitable and sustainable form of open access publishing. This study aimed to assess the awareness, perception and knowledge of DOA publishing practices among researchers in Ghana. A cross-sectional study design was used to conveniently collect data from 237 researchers across various institutions in Ghana. Data were collected using structured questionnaires Via Microsoft Forms and analysed using STATA version 17. Descriptive statistics, t-tests, ANOVA, factor analysis, Fisher’s exact test and logistic regression were conducted to identify patterns and relationships in the data. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05 with a 95% confidence interval. title: Janne Vilkuna kutsuttiin Kotiseutuliiton kunniapuheenjohtajaksi
content:
Suomen Kotiseutuliitto on kutsunut professori emeritus Janne Vilkunan liiton kunniapuheenjohtajaksi. Vilkuna toimi Kotiseutuliiton puheenjohtajana 12 vuoden ajan ja on tehnyt pitkän ja monipuolisen uran suomalaisen kotiseutu- ja kulttuuriperintötyön parissa. Hän on vasta toinen kunniapuheenjohtajaksi kutsuttu henkilö Kotiseutuliiton historiassa.

Kunniapuheenjohtajan mitali luovutettiin Vilkunalle lauantai-iltana Torniossa Kotiseutugaalassa, joka oli osa Tornion Valtakunnallisia kotiseutupäiviä.

Vilkuna toimi Kotiseutuliiton valtuustossa vuosina 2007–2025, aluksi yliopistoja edustavana asiantuntijajäsenenä. Valtuuston varapuheenjohtajana hän toimi vuosina 2009–2013 ja puheenjohtajana 2013–2025.

Pitkällä puheenjohtajakaudellaan Vilkuna vaikutti vahvasti Kotiseutuliiton toimintaan ja sen kehittämiseen. Hän työskenteli määrätietoisesti liiton tavoitteiden sekä kotiseututyön yhteistoiminnan ja yhteishengen vahvistamiseksi.

Vilkuna on museologian professori emeritus Jyväskylän yliopistosta. Hän työskenteli Keski-Suomen museossa 1980-luvulla ennen siirtymistään Jyväskylän yliopistoon. Museologian professorin tehtävän lisäksi hän toimi yliopiston museon johtajana.

title: 6 issues that will shape Ursula von der Leyen’s legacy
content:
With 3 years left in her term, the Commission boss must revive Europe’s industry, defend its rules, bolster security, support Ukraine, expand the bloc — and pay for it all.

By ZOYA SHEFTALOVICH
in Brussels

Illustration by Eva Redamonti for POLITICO

Ursula von der Leyen has three years left to cement her legacy, but it’ll be far from easy.

Von der Leyen’s second term ends in 2029, by which time she’ll have been at the helm of the European Commission for a decade. If, as Brussels Playbook reported earlier this summer, the EU executive chief won’t seek a third term, then she’s in the final stretch of her career in Brussels.

Her time in office has been dominated by crisis management — Covid-19, Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, sky-high energy prices, war in Gaza. In the years to come, the challenges will likely keep mounting, including competition from China and the United States, and upcoming elections in France, Spain, Italy and Poland that could reshape the EU.

title: Public Access, Open Access, and the Need for NIH Governance | Health Policy | JAMA Internal Medicine | JAMA Network
content: Abstract:  In July 2025, the National Institutes of Health (NIH) Public Access Policy took effect, marking a landmark commitment to free immediate access to taxpayer-funded research. The policy requires that author accepted manuscripts from NIH-funded research be made publicly available in PubMed Central (PMC) immediately on publication, replacing an earlier policy that allowed publishers a 12-month embargo between publication and free public access.1 Several of the largest publishers have responded by requiring NIH-funded authors to pay open access article processing charges (APCs) to deposit the article in PMC. Although the NIH has stated that compliance does not require APC payment,2 it has not publicly defended this position against publisher practices to the contrary. This Viewpoint examines the resulting confusion between public access and open access, the pay-to-comply publisher practices that conflate the two, and the steps that the NIH must take to fill this gap and promote its public access goals.

title: Stop paying predatory publishers of academic journals—A policy proposal to restore scientific integrity and transparency - Rainey - FEBS Letters - Wiley Online Library
content: Abstract:  Scientific publishing is undergoing a systemic breakdown. Thousands of journals now collect article processing charges (APCs)—increasingly paid from public research funds—while providing minimal editorial oversight. This erodes standards, distorts incentives and threatens public trust in science. APC payments to six major publishers exceeded 8 billion dollars between 2019 and 2023, with almost no transparency over how these fees are set or spent. This cannot continue. We propose that public and institutional funds support journals—whether through APCs, subscriptions or bundled agreements—only where they are accredited against a transparent, enforceable quality standard. Implemented in stages and led by funding bodies and learned societies, such accreditation would narrow the space in which predatory journals operate without resorting to blacklists.

    • Das Fediverse ist keine Plattform – es ist ein eigenes Universum. Es führt Microblogging und Longreads, Videoclips und Bilder, Podcasts und Musik und vieles mehr zusammen. Es läuft auf unterschiedlicher Software und wird von verschiedenen Communities betrieben, aber alle sind durch offene Protokolle miteinander verbunden. Was es zusammenhält, ist kein Unternehmen oder Geschäftsmodell – es ist ein gemeinsames Ideal davon, wie wir online kommunizieren und wer die Kontrolle darüber hat.

    Wir sind überzeugt davon, dass ein föderiertes und freies Netz der beste Weg ist, eine nachhaltige Alternative zu Big Tech zu etablieren. Nur so kann ein demokratischer Austausch ermöglicht werden, ohne auf Plattformen angewiesen zu sein, die in den Händen von gewinnorientierten Monopolisten liegen und uns mit algorithmisch generierten Timelines Werbung ausspielen und rechte Hetze in den Vordergrund rücken oder unliebsame Inhalte vorenthalten.

title: The devastating impact of copper and cobalt mining pollution in Lualaba, DRC
content:
Almost 98 percent of the study’s hourly measurements exceed the WHO safety thresholds

Originally published on Global Voices

A residential area beside a large industrial mining site. Photo by Afrewatch. Used with permission.

In the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), about 1,500 students and 68 staff members at the Galaxy School in Kolwezi breathe in some of the most polluted air ever recorded in this region. Their school sits less than 500 meters away from a mining waste disposal site.

Almost 98 percent of the hourly fine-particle levels exceed World Health Organization safety thresholds. This figure alone confirms what the latest scientific studies conducted in the Lualaba mining area have revealed.

The DRC is often hailed as a key player in the green energy transition, largely because the mineral resources within its borders are essential to producing batteries, solar panels, and other green tech. However, independent scientific studies on the scale of the contamination paint an alarming picture of the environmental cost in the Lualaba mining areas.

title: Vuosikokouksen julkilausuma: Uhkaako meitä yhteisöllinen muistisairaus?
content:
Nykyisenkaltaisena kriisiaikana kulttuuriperinnön arvo korostuu: huomaamme selvemmin, mitä me haluamme säilyttää ja puolustaa. Paikallista kulttuuriperintöä ylläpitävät monesti vapaaehtoiset, pienin resurssein ja suurella sydämellä. Tämä työ jää syrjään kansallisesta katseesta. Niin ei tulisi olla.

Naapurustoilla ja kortteleilla, kylillä ja kaupunginosilla, kunnilla ja kaupungeilla on omat muistonsa ja oma muistinsa. Paikallinen muisti elää rakennuksissa ja esineissä, perinteissä ja tapahtumissa, valokuvissa ja asiakirjoissa. Se kertoo, kuinka eteenpäin on menty ja vaikeuksista selvitty yhdessä.

Perhepiirissä heräämme monesti vasta liian myöhään huomaamaan menneisyyden arvon. Historia alkaa usein kiinnostaa vasta aikuisiässä. Silloin esineiden tarinoita tai valokuvien henkilöitä ei ehkä enää tunneta eikä ole ketään keneltä kysyä.

title: Haiti’s security crisis forces displacement and relocation
content:
‘I am very grateful to be here and finally able to rest with dignity’

Originally published on Global Voices

Feature image of a Haitian flag and fist raised in resistance created using Canva Pro elements.

Haiti’s Centre Department (Plateau Central) lies between the West Departments and the Great North of the country, covering an area of about 3,487 square kilometres (about 2,166 square miles).

The communes of Saut d’Eau and Mirebalais are famous for their major religious festivals, musical events, and large religious ceremonies. People from all over used to visit the Catholic church there. Every July 16, Saut d’Eau celebrates Notre Dame du Mont Carmel (also called Vyèj Mirak Sodo), with the big activities usually starting in mid-July. Many pilgrims travel to the area to bathe in the waterfall it’s named after, pray to the saint, attend large Vodou ceremonies, and enjoy cultural events.
